gata-saṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthita-cetasaḥ | yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṁ pravilīyate ||23||
docs.text: For one who is free from attachment, who is liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge, and who acts only as a sacrifice — all karma dissolves entirely.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.23

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: brahma arpaṇam brahma haviḥ brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam brahma eva tena gantavyam brahma-karma-samādhinā
brahmārpaṇaṁ brahma havir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam | brahmaiva tena gantavyaṁ brahma-karma-samādhinā ||24||
docs.text: The act of offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, offered by Brahman into the fire of Brahman. Brahman alone is to be reached by one who sees Brahman in every action.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.24

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: daivam eva apare yajñam yoginaḥ paryupāsate brahmāgnau apare yajñena eva upajuhvati
daivam evāpare yajñaṁ yoginaḥ paryupāsate | brahmāgnāv apare yajñaṁ yajñenaivopajuhvati ||25||
docs.text: Some yogis perform sacrifice by worshipping the gods alone; others offer the sacrifice itself as an oblation into the fire of Brahman.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.25

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śrotrādīni indriyāṇi anye saṁyama agniṣu juhvati śabdādīn viṣayān indriyāgniṣu
śrotrādīnīndriyāṇy anye saṁyamāgniṣu juhvati | śabdādīn viṣayān anye indriyāgniṣu juhvati ||26||
docs.text: Some offer the senses such as hearing into the fires of self-restraint; others offer sense objects such as sound into the fires of the senses.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.26

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: sarvāṇi indriya-karmāṇi prāṇa-karmāṇi ca apare ātma-saṁyama-yogāgnau juhvati jñāna-dīpite
sarvāṇīndriya-karmāṇi prāṇa-karmāṇi cāpare | ātma-saṁyama-yogāgnau juhvati jñāna-dīpite ||27||
docs.text: Others offer all the functions of the senses and the functions of the life-breath into the fire of the yoga of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.27

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: dravya-yajñās tapo-yajñā yoga-yajñās tathāpare | svādhyāya-jñāna-yajñāś ca yatayaḥ saṁśita-vratāḥ ||28||
dravya-yajñāḥ tapo-yajñāḥ yoga-yajñāḥ tathā apare svādhyāya jñāna-yajñāḥ ca yatayaḥ saṁśita-vratāḥ
docs.text: Some offer their wealth as sacrifice, some offer austerity, some offer yoga, and others — ascetics of strict vows — offer self-study and knowledge as their sacrifice.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.28

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: apāne juhvati prāṇam prāṇe apānam tathā apare prāṇāpāna-gatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāma-parāyaṇāḥ
apāne juhvati prāṇaṁ prāṇe 'pānaṁ tathāpare | prāṇāpāna-gatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāma-parāyaṇāḥ ||29||
docs.text: Still others offer the outgoing breath into the incoming breath, and the incoming breath into the outgoing breath, restraining the movement of both — devoted to the practice of pranayama (breath control).
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.29

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati sarve api ete yajña-vidaḥ yajña-kṣapita-kalmaṣāḥ
apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati | sarve 'py ete yajña-vido yajña-kṣapita-kalmaṣāḥ ||30||
docs.text: Others, who regulate their diet, offer the life-breaths into the life-breaths. All of these are knowers of sacrifice, and their sins are destroyed through sacrifice.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.30

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yajña-śiṣṭa amṛta bhujaḥ yānti brahma sanātanam na ayam lokaḥ asti ayajñasya kutaḥ anyaḥ kuru-sattama
yajña-śiṣṭāmṛta-bhujo yānti brahma sanātanam | nāyaṁ loko 'sty ayajñasya kuto 'nyaḥ kuru-sattama ||31||
docs.text: Those who partake of the nectar of the remnants of sacrifice attain the eternal Brahman. Even this world is not for one who makes no sacrifice — how then any other world, O best of the Kurus?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.31

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: evam bahu-vidhāḥ yajñāḥ vitatāḥ brahmaṇaḥ mukhe karma-jān viddhi tān sarvān jñātvā vimokṣyase
evaṁ bahu-vidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe | karma-jān viddhi tān sarvān evaṁ jñātvā vimokṣyase ||32||
docs.text: Thus, many kinds of sacrifices are described in the Vedas. Know them all to be born of action. Knowing this, you shall be liberated.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.32

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śreyān dravya-mayād yajñāj jñāna-yajñaḥ parantapa | sarvaṁ karmākhilaṁ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate ||33||
śreyān dravya-mayāt yajñāt jñāna-yajñaḥ parantapa sarvam karma akhilam pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate
docs.text: The sacrifice of knowledge is superior to any material sacrifice, O scorcher of foes. All actions in their entirety, O Partha, culminate in knowledge.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.33

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: tad viddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā | upadekṣyanti te jñānaṁ jñāninas tattva-darśinaḥ ||34||
tat viddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā upadekṣyanti te jñānam jñāninaḥ tattva-darśinaḥ
docs.text: Learn that by prostrating yourself, by asking questions, and by rendering service. The wise ones, the seers of truth, will impart knowledge to you.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.34

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yaj jñātvā na punar moham evaṁ yāsyasi pāṇḍava | yena bhūtāny aśeṣeṇa drakṣyasy ātmany atho mayi ||35||
yat jñātvā na punaḥ moham yāsyasi pāṇḍava yena bhūtāni aśeṣeṇa drakṣyasi ātmani atho mayi
docs.text: Knowing which, you shall not again fall into delusion, O Pandava. By that knowledge, you shall see all beings without exception in the Self, and then in Me.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.35

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: api ced asi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpa-kṛttamaḥ | sarvaṁ jñāna-plavenaiva vṛjinaṁ santariṣyasi ||36||
api cet asi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpa-kṛttamaḥ sarvam jñāna-plavena eva vṛjinam santariṣyasi
docs.text: Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners, you shall cross over all sin by the raft of knowledge alone.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.36

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yathaidhāṁsi samiddho 'gnir bhasmasāt kurute 'rjuna | jñānāgniḥ sarva-karmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute tathā ||37||
yathā edhāṁsi samiddhaḥ agniḥ bhasmasāt kurute arjuna jñānāgniḥ sarva-karmāṇi tathā
docs.text: Just as a blazing fire reduces firewood to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge reduce all karma to ashes.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.37

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: na hi jñānena sadṛśam pavitram iha vidyate tat svayam yoga-saṁsiddhaḥ kālena ātmani vindati
na hi jñānena sadṛśaṁ pavitram iha vidyate | tat svayaṁ yoga-saṁsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati ||38||
docs.text: In this world, there is nothing as purifying as knowledge. One who is perfected in yoga finds that knowledge spontaneously in the Self, in due course of time.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.38

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śraddhāvān labhate jñānam tat-paraḥ saṁyatendriyaḥ labdhvā parām śāntim acireṇa adhigacchati
śraddhāvāṁl labhate jñānaṁ tat-paraḥ saṁyatendriyaḥ | jñānaṁ labdhvā parāṁ śāntim acireṇādhigacchati ||39||
docs.text: The faithful one, devoted to knowledge and having mastered the senses, attains knowledge. Having attained knowledge, one quickly reaches supreme peace.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.39

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: ajñaś cāśraddadhānaś ca saṁśayātmā vinaśyati | nāyaṁ loko 'sti na paro na sukhaṁ saṁśayātmanaḥ ||40||
ajñaḥ ca aśraddadhānaḥ saṁśayātmā vinaśyati na ayam lokaḥ paraḥ sukham saṁśayātmanaḥ
docs.text: The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubter perish. For the doubting soul, there is neither this world, nor the next, nor any happiness.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.40

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yoga-sannyasta-karmāṇam jñāna-sañchinna-saṁśayam ātmavantam na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya
yoga-sannyasta-karmāṇaṁ jñāna-sañchinna-saṁśayam | ātmavantaṁ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya ||41||
docs.text: One who has renounced actions through yoga, whose doubts have been destroyed by knowledge, and who is self-possessed — actions do not bind such a person, O Dhananjaya.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.41

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: tasmād ajñāna-sambhūtaṁ hṛt-sthaṁ jñānāsinātmanaḥ | chittvainaṁ saṁśayaṁ yogam ātiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhārata ||42||
tasmāt ajñāna-sambhūtam hṛt-stham jñānāsinā ātmanaḥ chittvā enam saṁśayam yogam ātiṣṭha uttiṣṭha bhārata
docs.text: Therefore, with the sword of knowledge, cut asunder the doubt born of ignorance residing in your heart. Take refuge in yoga. Arise, O Bharata!
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 4.42

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: arjuna uvāca sannyāsam karmaṇām kṛṣṇa punaḥ yogam ca śaṁsasi yat śreyaḥ etayoḥ ekam tat me brūhi suniścitam
arjuna uvāca | sannyāsaṁ karmaṇāṁ kṛṣṇa punar yogaṁ ca śaṁsasi | yac chreya etayor ekaṁ tan me brūhi suniścitam ||1||
docs.text: Arjuna said: O Krishna, you praise renunciation of actions and also yoga (selfless action). Tell me with certainty which one of these two is better.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.1

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śrī bhagavān uvāca sannyāsaḥ karma-yogaḥ ca niḥśreyasa-karau ubhau tayoḥ tu karma-sannyāsāt karma-yogaḥ viśiṣyate
śrī bhagavān uvāca | sannyāsaḥ karma-yogaś ca niḥśreyasa-karāv ubhau | tayos tu karma-sannyāsāt karma-yogo viśiṣyate ||2||
docs.text: The Supreme Lord said: Both renunciation of actions and the yoga of action lead to liberation. But of the two, the yoga of action is superior to the renunciation of action.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.2

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: jñeyaḥ sa nitya-sannyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati | nirdvandvo hi mahā-bāho sukhaṁ bandhāt pramucyate ||3||
jñeyaḥ saḥ nitya-sannyāsī yaḥ na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati nirdvandvaḥ hi mahā-bāho sukham bandhāt pramucyate
docs.text: He who neither hates nor desires should be known as a perpetual renunciant. Free from dualities, O mighty-armed Arjuna, he is easily liberated from bondage.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.3

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: sāṅkhya-yogau pṛthag bālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ | ekam apy āsthitaḥ samyag ubhayor vindate phalam ||4||
sāṅkhya-yogau pṛthak bālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ ekam api āsthitaḥ samyak ubhayoḥ vindate phalam
docs.text: Only the ignorant speak of Sankhya (path of knowledge) and Yoga (path of action) as different, not the wise. One who is properly established in even one of them obtains the fruit of both.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.4

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yat sāṅkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānam tat yogaiḥ api gamyate ekam sāṅkhyam ca yogam yaḥ paśyati saḥ paśyati
yat sāṅkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṁ tad yogair api gamyate | ekaṁ sāṅkhyaṁ ca yogaṁ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati ||5||
docs.text: The state that is reached by the followers of Sankhya is also reached by the practitioners of Yoga. He who sees Sankhya and Yoga as one — he truly sees.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.5

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: sannyāsas tu mahā-bāho duḥkham āptum ayogataḥ | yoga-yukto munir brahma nacireṇādhigacchati ||6||
sannyāsaḥ tu mahā-bāho duḥkham āptum ayogataḥ yoga-yuktaḥ muniḥ brahma nacireṇa adhigacchati
docs.text: But renunciation, O mighty-armed Arjuna, is difficult to attain without yoga. The sage who is united in yoga quickly attains Brahman.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.6

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yoga-yuktaḥ viśuddha-ātmā vijita-ātmā jita-indriyaḥ sarva-bhūta-ātma-bhūta-ātmā kurvan api na lipyate
yoga-yukto viśuddhātmā vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ | sarva-bhūtātma-bhūtātmā kurvann api na lipyate ||7||
docs.text: He who is united in yoga, whose self is purified, who has conquered the mind and mastered the senses, and who sees the Self in all beings — though he acts, he is not tainted.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.7

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: na eva kiñcit karomi iti yuktaḥ manyeta tattva-vit paśyan śṛṇvan spṛśan jighran aśnan gacchan svapan śvasan
naiva kiñcit karomīti yukto manyeta tattva-vit | paśyañ śṛṇvan spṛśañ jighran naśnan gacchan svapañ śvasan ||8||
docs.text: The knower of truth, though seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping, and breathing, should think 'I do nothing at all.'
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.8

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: pralapan visṛjan gṛhṇan unmiṣan nimiṣan api indriyāṇi indriya-artheṣu vartante iti dhārayan
pralapan visṛjan gṛhṇann unmiṣan nimiṣann api | indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan ||9||
docs.text: Speaking, letting go, grasping, opening and closing the eyes — the knower of truth holds the conviction that it is merely the senses engaging with their objects.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.9

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: brahmaṇi ādhāya karmāṇi saṅgam tyaktvā karoti yaḥ lipyate na saḥ pāpena padma-patram iva ambhasā
brahmaṇy ādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padma-patram ivāmbhasā ||10||
docs.text: He who performs actions offering them to Brahman, abandoning all attachment, is not tainted by sin — just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.10

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalair indriyair api | yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṁ tyaktvātma-śuddhaye ||11||
kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalaiḥ indriyaiḥ api yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgam tyaktvā ātma-śuddhaye
docs.text: Yogis perform action with the body, mind, intellect, and even with the senses alone, abandoning attachment, for the purification of the self.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.11

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yuktaḥ karma-phalam tyaktvā śāntim āpnoti naiṣṭhikīm ayuktaḥ kāma-kāreṇa phale saktaḥ nibadhyate
yuktaḥ karma-phalaṁ tyaktvā śāntim āpnoti naiṣṭhikīm | ayuktaḥ kāma-kāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate ||12||
docs.text: The disciplined one, having abandoned the fruit of action, attains lasting peace. The undisciplined one, driven by desire and attached to the fruit, is bound.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.12

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: sarva-karmāṇi manasā sannyasya āste sukham vaśī nava-dvāre pure dehī na eva kurvan na kārayan
sarva-karmāṇi manasā sannyasyāste sukhaṁ vaśī | nava-dvāre pure dehī naiva kurvan na kārayan ||13||
docs.text: The self-controlled embodied soul, having mentally renounced all actions, rests happily in the city of nine gates — neither acting nor causing action.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.13

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: na kartṛtvam na karmāṇi lokasya sṛjati prabhuḥ na karma-phala-saṁyogam svabhāvaḥ tu pravartate
na kartṛtvaṁ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛjati prabhuḥ | na karma-phala-saṁyogaṁ svabhāvas tu pravartate ||14||
docs.text: The Lord creates neither the sense of doership nor the actions of people, nor the connection between action and its fruit. It is one's own nature that operates.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.14

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: na ādatte kasyacit pāpam na ca eva sukṛtam vibhuḥ ajñānena āvṛtam jñānam tena muhyanti jantavaḥ
nādatte kasyacit pāpaṁ na caiva sukṛtaṁ vibhuḥ | ajñānenāvṛtaṁ jñānaṁ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ ||15||
docs.text: The all-pervading Lord takes neither the sin nor the merit of anyone. Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and by that, living beings are deluded.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.15

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: jñānena tu tad ajñānaṁ yeṣāṁ nāśitam ātmanaḥ | teṣām āditya-vaj jñānaṁ prakāśayati tat param ||16||
jñānena tu tat ajñānam yeṣām nāśitam ātmanaḥ teṣām āditya-vat jñānam prakāśayati tat param
docs.text: But for those whose ignorance of the self is destroyed by knowledge, that knowledge, like the sun, illuminates the Supreme Truth.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.16

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: tad-buddhayas tad-ātmānas tan-niṣṭhās tat-parāyaṇāḥ | gacchanty apunar-āvṛttiṁ jñāna-nirdhūta-kalmaṣāḥ ||17||
tad-buddhayaḥ tad-ātmānaḥ tan-niṣṭhāḥ tat-parāyaṇāḥ gacchanti apunar-āvṛttim jñāna-nirdhūta-kalmaṣāḥ
docs.text: Those whose intellect is absorbed in That, whose self is identified with That, who are firmly established in That, and who have That as their supreme refuge — they go to the state of no return, their sins washed away by knowledge.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.17

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: vidyā-vinaya-sampanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini | śuni caiva śva-pāke ca paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśinaḥ ||18||
vidyā-vinaya-sampanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini śuni ca eva śva-pāke ca paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśinaḥ
docs.text: The wise see with equal vision a learned and humble Brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and even an outcaste.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.18

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: iha eva taiḥ jitaḥ sargaḥ yeṣām sāmye sthitam manaḥ nirdoṣam hi samam brahma tasmāt brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ
ihaiva tair jitaḥ sargo yeṣāṁ sāmye sthitaṁ manaḥ | nirdoṣaṁ hi samaṁ brahma tasmād brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ ||19||
docs.text: Even here in this world, creation is conquered by those whose minds are established in equality. Brahman is flawless and impartial; therefore, they are established in Brahman.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.19

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: na prahṛṣyet priyam prāpya na udvijet prāpya ca apriyam sthira-buddhiḥ asammūḍhaḥ brahma-vit brahmaṇi sthitaḥ
na prahṛṣyet priyaṁ prāpya nodvijet prāpya cāpriyam | sthira-buddhir asammūḍho brahma-vid brahmaṇi sthitaḥ ||20||
docs.text: One should neither rejoice upon obtaining what is pleasant, nor be disturbed upon obtaining what is unpleasant. With steady intellect and undeluded, the knower of Brahman is established in Brahman.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.20

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: bāhya sparśeṣu asakta-ātmā vindati ātmani yat sukham saḥ brahma-yoga-yukta-ātmā sukham akṣayam aśnute
bāhya-sparśeṣv asaktātmā vindaty ātmani yat sukham | sa brahma-yoga-yuktātmā sukham akṣayam aśnute ||21||
docs.text: One whose self is unattached to external sense contacts finds happiness in the Self. With the self united with Brahman through yoga, such a person attains imperishable bliss.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.21

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: ye hi saṁsparśa-jā bhogā duḥkha-yonaya eva te | ādy-antavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣu ramate budhaḥ ||22||
ye hi saṁsparśa-jāḥ bhogāḥ duḥkha-yonayaḥ eva te ādy-antavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣu ramate budhaḥ
docs.text: The pleasures born of sense contact are indeed sources of sorrow alone. They have a beginning and an end, O son of Kunti. The wise person does not delight in them.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.22

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śaknoti ihaiva yaḥ soḍhum prāk śarīra-vimokṣaṇāt kāma-krodha-udbhavam vegam saḥ yuktaḥ saḥ sukhī naraḥ
śaknotīhaiva yaḥ soḍhuṁ prāk śarīra-vimokṣaṇāt | kāma-krodhodbhavaṁ vegaṁ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ ||23||
docs.text: One who is able to withstand, here in this life before death, the impulse born of desire and anger — that person is a yogi, that person is truly happy.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.23

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yaḥ antaḥ-sukhaḥ antar-ārāmaḥ tathā antar-jyotiḥ eva yaḥ saḥ yogī brahma-nirvāṇam brahma-bhūtaḥ adhigacchati
yo 'ntaḥ-sukho 'ntar-ārāmas tathāntar-jyotir eva yaḥ | sa yogī brahma-nirvāṇaṁ brahma-bhūto 'dhigacchati ||24||
docs.text: One whose happiness is within, who rejoices within, and whose light is within — that yogi, having become one with Brahman, attains liberation in Brahman.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.24

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: labhante brahma-nirvāṇam ṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇa-kalmaṣāḥ chinna-dvaidhāḥ yata-ātmānaḥ sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ
labhante brahma-nirvāṇam ṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇa-kalmaṣāḥ | chinna-dvaidhā yatātmānaḥ sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ ||25||
docs.text: The sages whose sins are destroyed, whose doubts are cut asunder, whose minds are disciplined, and who are devoted to the welfare of all beings — they attain liberation in Brahman.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.25

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: kāma-krodha-viyuktānām yatīnām yata-cetasām abhitaḥ brahma-nirvāṇam vartate vidita-ātmanām
kāma-krodha-viyuktānāṁ yatīnāṁ yata-cetasām | abhito brahma-nirvāṇaṁ vartate viditātmanām ||26||
docs.text: For those ascetics who are free from desire and anger, who have controlled their minds and realized the Self — liberation in Brahman exists everywhere, on all sides.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.26

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: sparśān kṛtvā bahir bāhyāṁś cakṣuś caivāntare bhruvoḥ | prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā nāsābhyantara-cāriṇau ||27||
sparśān kṛtvā bahiḥ bāhyān cakṣuḥ ca eva antare bhruvoḥ prāṇa-apānau samau kṛtvā nāsa-abhyantara-cāriṇau
docs.text: Shutting out all external sense contacts, fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, equalizing the outgoing and incoming breaths moving within the nostrils —
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.27

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yata-indriya-mano-buddhiḥ muniḥ mokṣa-parāyaṇaḥ vigata-icchā-bhaya-krodhaḥ yaḥ sadā muktaḥ eva saḥ
yatendriya-mano-buddhir munir mokṣa-parāyaṇaḥ | vigatecchā-bhaya-krodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ ||28||
docs.text: — the sage who has controlled senses, mind, and intellect, who is devoted to liberation, and who is free from desire, fear, and anger — such a person is forever liberated indeed.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.28

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: bhoktāram yajña-tapasām sarva-loka-maheśvaram suhṛdam sarva-bhūtānām jñātvā mām śāntim ṛcchati
bhoktāraṁ yajña-tapasāṁ sarva-loka-maheśvaram | suhṛdaṁ sarva-bhūtānāṁ jñātvā māṁ śāntim ṛcchati ||29||
docs.text: Knowing Me as the enjoyer of all sacrifices and austerities, the great Lord of all worlds, and the selfless friend of all living beings — one attains peace.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 5.29

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śrī bhagavān uvāca anāśritaḥ karma-phalam kāryam karma karoti yaḥ saḥ sannyāsī yogī na niragniḥ akriyaḥ
śrī bhagavān uvāca | anāśritaḥ karma-phalaṁ kāryaṁ karma karoti yaḥ | sa sannyāsī ca yogī ca na niragnir na cākriyaḥ ||1||
docs.text: The Supreme Lord said: One who performs their prescribed duty without depending on the fruits of action is a true sannyasi and yogi — not one who merely gives up the sacred fire or ceases all activity.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.1

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yam sannyāsam iti prāhuḥ yogam tam viddhi pāṇḍava na hi asannyasta-saṅkalpaḥ yogī bhavati kaścana
yaṁ sannyāsam iti prāhur yogaṁ taṁ viddhi pāṇḍava | na hy asannyasta-saṅkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana ||2||
docs.text: What they call renunciation, know that to be yoga, O Pandava. For no one becomes a yogi without renouncing selfish desires and intentions.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.2

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: ārurukṣor muner yogaṁ karma kāraṇam ucyate | yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva śamaḥ kāraṇam ucyate ||3||
ārurukṣoḥ muneḥ yogam karma kāraṇam ucyate yogārūḍhasya tasya eva śamaḥ
docs.text: For a sage who is aspiring to attain yoga, action is said to be the means. For one who has already attained yoga, tranquility (cessation of selfish action) is said to be the means.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.3

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yadā hi na indriyārtheṣu karmasu anuṣajjate sarva-saṅkalpa-sannyāsī yogārūḍhaḥ tadā ucyate
yadā hi nendriyārtheṣu na karmasv anuṣajjate | sarva-saṅkalpa-sannyāsī yogārūḍhas tadocyate ||4||
docs.text: When one is attached neither to sense objects nor to actions, and has renounced all selfish desires, then one is said to be established in yoga.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.4

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: uddhared ātmanātmānaṁ nātmānam avasādayet | ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ ||5||
uddharet ātmanā ātmānam na avasādayet ātmā eva hi ātmanaḥ bandhuḥ ripuḥ
docs.text: One must elevate oneself by one's own mind, and not degrade oneself. The mind alone is the friend of the self, and the mind alone is the enemy of the self.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.5

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: bandhur ātmātmanas tasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanas tu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||6||
bandhuḥ ātmā ātmanaḥ tasya yena ātmanā jitaḥ anātmanaḥ tu śatrutve varteta śatruvat
docs.text: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. But for one who has failed to do so, the mind remains the greatest enemy, behaving like a foe.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.6

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya paramātmā samāhitaḥ | śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu tathā mānāpamānayoḥ ||7||
jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya paramātmā samāhitaḥ śīta uṣṇa sukha duḥkheṣu māna apamānayoḥ
docs.text: For one who has conquered the mind and is peaceful, the Supreme Self is already reached. Such a person remains steady in cold and heat, happiness and sorrow, honor and dishonor.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.7

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: jñāna vijñāna tṛptātmā kūṭasthaḥ vijitendriyaḥ yuktaḥ iti ucyate yogī sama-loṣṭa-aśma-kāñcanaḥ
jñāna-vijñāna-tṛptātmā kūṭastho vijitendriyaḥ | yukta ity ucyate yogī sama-loṣṭāśma-kāñcanaḥ ||8||
docs.text: One who is satisfied with knowledge and realization, who is steady and has conquered the senses, is called a yogi. To such a person, a clod of earth, a stone, and gold are the same.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.8

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: suhṛn-mitrāry-udāsīna-madhyastha-dveṣya-bandhuṣu | sādhuṣv api ca pāpeṣu sama-buddhir viśiṣyate ||9||
suhṛt mitra ari udāsīna madhyastha dveṣya bandhuṣu sādhuṣu api ca pāpeṣu sama-buddhiḥ viśiṣyate
docs.text: One who regards with equal mind well-wishers, friends, enemies, the indifferent, neutrals, the hateful, relatives, the righteous, and even the sinful — such a person excels.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.9

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yogī yuñjīta satatam ātmānam rahasi sthitaḥ ekākī yata-cittātmā nirāśīḥ aparigrahaḥ
yogī yuñjīta satatam ātmānaṁ rahasi sthitaḥ | ekākī yata-cittātmā nirāśīr aparigrahaḥ ||10||
docs.text: The yogi should constantly engage the mind in meditation, remaining in a secluded place, alone, with mind and body controlled, free from desires and possessiveness.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.10

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiram āsanam ātmanaḥ na atyucchritam atinīcam caila ajina kuśa uttaram
śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiram āsanam ātmanaḥ | nātyucchritaṁ nātinīcaṁ cailājina-kuśottaram ||11||
docs.text: In a clean place, having established a firm seat for oneself, neither too high nor too low, covered with cloth, deerskin, and kusha grass —
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.11

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: tatra ekāgram manaḥ kṛtvā yata citta indriya kriyaḥ upaviśya āsane yuñjyāt yogam ātma-viśuddhaye
tatraikāgraṁ manaḥ kṛtvā yata-cittendriya-kriyaḥ | upaviśyāsane yuñjyād yogam ātma-viśuddhaye ||12||
docs.text: Sitting there on the seat, making the mind one-pointed, with the activities of thought and senses controlled, one should practice yoga for the purification of the self.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.12

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: samam kāya śiraḥ grīvam dhārayan acalam sthiraḥ samprekṣya nāsikāgram svam diśaḥ ca anavalokayan
samaṁ kāya-śiro-grīvaṁ dhārayann acalaṁ sthiraḥ | sampreksya nāsikāgraṁ svaṁ diśaś cānavalokayan ||13||
docs.text: Holding the body, head, and neck erect and still, gazing steadily at the tip of one's own nose, not looking around in any direction —
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.13

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: praśāntātmā vigata-bhīr brahmacāri-vrate sthitaḥ | manaḥ saṁyamya mac-citto yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ ||14||
praśāntātmā vigata-bhīḥ brahmacāri-vrate sthitaḥ manaḥ saṁyamya mac-cittaḥ yuktaḥ āsīta mat-paraḥ
docs.text: Serene, fearless, firm in the vow of celibacy, with the mind controlled and thoughts fixed on Me, the yogi should sit in meditation, devoted to Me as the supreme goal.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.14

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yuñjan evam sadā ātmānam yogī niyata-mānasaḥ śāntim nirvāṇa-paramām mat-saṁsthām adhigacchati
yuñjann evaṁ sadātmānaṁ yogī niyata-mānasaḥ | śāntiṁ nirvāṇa-paramāṁ mat-saṁsthām adhigacchati ||15||
docs.text: Thus, always keeping the mind engaged in yoga, with a controlled mind, the yogi attains the peace of supreme nirvana — the ultimate liberation that abides in Me.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.15

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: na atyaśnataḥ tu yogaḥ asti na ca ekāntam anaśnataḥ na atisvapnaśīlasya jāgrataḥ na eva arjuna
nātyaśnatas tu yogo 'sti na caikāntam anaśnataḥ | na cātisvapnaśīlasya jāgrato naiva cārjuna ||16||
docs.text: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or too little, nor for one who sleeps too much or stays awake too long, O Arjuna.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.16

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yukta āhāra vihārasya yukta-ceṣṭasya karmasu yukta svapna avabodhasya yogaḥ bhavati duḥkhahā
yuktāhāra-vihārasya yukta-ceṣṭasya karmasu | yukta-svapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkhahā ||17||
docs.text: For one who is regulated in eating, recreation, effort in work, and regulated in sleep and wakefulness — yoga becomes the destroyer of all sorrow.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.17

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yadā viniyatam cittam ātmani eva avatiṣṭhate niḥspṛhaḥ sarva-kāmebhyaḥ yuktaḥ iti ucyate tadā
yadā viniyataṁ cittam ātmany evāvatiṣṭhate | niḥspṛhaḥ sarva-kāmebhyo yukta ity ucyate tadā ||18||
docs.text: When the perfectly disciplined mind rests in the Self alone, free from longing for all desires, then one is said to be 'yukta' — established in yoga.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.18

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yathā dīpaḥ nivāta-sthaḥ na iṅgate sā upamā smṛtā yoginaḥ yata-cittasya yuñjataḥ yogam ātmanaḥ
yathā dīpo nivāta-stho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā | yogino yata-cittasya yuñjato yogam ātmanaḥ ||19||
docs.text: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker — that is the simile used to describe the yogi of controlled mind, practicing yoga of the Self.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.19

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yatra uparamate cittam niruddham yoga-sevayā yatra ātmanā ātmānam paśyan ātmani tuṣyati
yatroparamate cittaṁ niruddhaṁ yoga-sevayā | yatra caivātmanātmānaṁ paśyann ātmani tuṣyati ||20||
docs.text: Where the mind, restrained by the practice of yoga, finds rest; and where, seeing the Self by the self, one is satisfied in the Self alone.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.20

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: sukham ātyantikam yat tat buddhi-grāhyam atīndriyam vetti yatra na calati sthitaḥ tattvataḥ
sukham ātyantikaṁ yat tad buddhi-grāhyam atīndriyam | vetti yatra na caivāyaṁ sthitaś calati tattvataḥ ||21||
docs.text: That infinite happiness which is grasped by the intellect and is beyond the reach of the senses — established in that state, one never departs from the truth.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.21

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yam labdhvā aparam lābham manyate na adhikam tataḥ yasmin sthitaḥ na duḥkhena guruṇā api vicālyate
yaṁ labdhvā cāparaṁ lābhaṁ manyate nādhikaṁ tataḥ | yasmin sthito na duḥkhena guruṇāpi vicālyate ||22||
docs.text: Having gained that, one considers no other gain to be greater. Established therein, one is not shaken even by the heaviest sorrow.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.22

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: tam vidyāt duḥkha-saṁyoga viyogam yoga-saṁjñitam saḥ niścayena yoktavyaḥ yogaḥ anirviṇṇa-cetasā
taṁ vidyād duḥkha-saṁyoga-viyogaṁ yoga-saṁjñitam | sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo 'nirviṇṇa-cetasā ||23||
docs.text: That disconnection from union with sorrow should be known as yoga. This yoga should be practiced with determination and with an undismayed mind.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.23

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: saṅkalpa prabhavān kāmān tyaktvā sarvān aśeṣataḥ manasā eva indriya-grāmam viniyamya samantataḥ
saṅkalpa-prabhavān kāmāṁs tyaktvā sarvān aśeṣataḥ | manasaivendriya-grāmaṁ viniyamya samantataḥ ||24||
docs.text: Abandoning completely all desires born of sankalpa (imagination/mental resolve), and restraining the entire group of senses from all sides by the mind alone.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.24

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śanaiḥ śanair uparamed buddhyā dhṛti-gṛhītayā | ātma-saṁsthaṁ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiñcid api cintayet ||25||
śanaiḥ śanaiḥ uparamet buddhyā dhṛti-gṛhītayā ātma-saṁstham manaḥ kṛtvā na kiñcit api cintayet
docs.text: Gradually, step by step, one should attain tranquility through the intellect held by firm conviction. Having established the mind in the Self, one should not think of anything else.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.25

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yataḥ yataḥ niścarati manaḥ cañcalam asthiram tataḥ tataḥ niyamya etat ātmani eva vaśam nayet
yato yato niścarati manaś cañcalam asthiram | tatas tato niyamyaitad ātmany eva vaśaṁ nayet ||26||
docs.text: Wherever the restless and unsteady mind wanders, one should bring it back from there and place it under the control of the Self alone.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.26

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: praśānta manasam hi enam yoginam sukham uttamam upaiti śānta-rajasam brahma-bhūtam akalmaṣam
praśānta-manasaṁ hy enaṁ yoginaṁ sukham uttamam | upaiti śānta-rajasaṁ brahma-bhūtam akalmaṣam ||27||
docs.text: Supreme bliss comes to the yogi whose mind is peaceful, whose passions are calmed, who is sinless, and who has become one with Brahman.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.27

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yuñjan evam sadā ātmānam yogī vigata-kalmaṣaḥ sukhena brahma-saṁsparśam atyantam sukham aśnute
yuñjann evaṁ sadātmānaṁ yogī vigata-kalmaṣaḥ | sukhena brahma-saṁsparśam atyantaṁ sukham aśnute ||28||
docs.text: The yogi who is free from sin, constantly engaging the self in yoga, easily enjoys the infinite bliss of contact with Brahman.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.28

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: sarva-bhūta-stham ātmānam sarva-bhūtāni ca ātmani īkṣate yoga-yuktātmā sarvatra sama-darśanaḥ
sarva-bhūta-stham ātmānaṁ sarva-bhūtāni cātmani | īkṣate yoga-yuktātmā sarvatra sama-darśanaḥ ||29||
docs.text: One whose self is established in yoga sees the Self existing in all beings and all beings existing in the Self — seeing the same everywhere.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.29

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yaḥ mām paśyati sarvatra sarvam ca mayi paśyati tasya aham na praṇaśyāmi saḥ ca me na praṇaśyati
yo māṁ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṁ ca mayi paśyati | tasyāhaṁ na praṇaśyāmi sa ca me na praṇaśyati ||30||
docs.text: One who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me — I am never lost to them, nor are they ever lost to Me.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.30

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: sarva-bhūta-sthitam yaḥ mām bhajati ekatvam āsthitaḥ sarvathā vartamānaḥ api saḥ yogī mayi vartate
sarva-bhūta-sthitaṁ yo māṁ bhajaty ekatvam āsthitaḥ | sarvathā vartamāno 'pi sa yogī mayi vartate ||31||
docs.text: The yogi who, established in oneness, worships Me dwelling in all beings — that yogi abides in Me, regardless of how they live.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.31

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: ātma-aupamyena sarvatra samam paśyati yaḥ arjuna sukham vā yadi duḥkham saḥ yogī paramaḥ mataḥ
ātmaupamyena sarvatra samaṁ paśyati yo 'rjuna | sukhaṁ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṁ sa yogī paramo mataḥ ||32||
docs.text: One who, by comparison with oneself, sees equality everywhere — in the happiness and sorrow of all beings, O Arjuna — that yogi is considered the highest.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.32

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: arjuna uvāca yaḥ ayam yogaḥ tvayā proktaḥ sāmyena madhusūdana etasya aham na paśyāmi cañcalatvāt sthitim sthirām
arjuna uvāca | yo 'yaṁ yogas tvayā proktaḥ sāmyena madhusūdana | etasyāhaṁ na paśyāmi cañcalatvāt sthitiṁ sthirām ||33||
docs.text: Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, this yoga of equanimity that You have described — I do not see how it can endure steadily, because the mind is so restless.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.33

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: cañcalam hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavat dṛḍham tasya aham nigraham manye vāyoḥ iva suduṣkaram
cañcalaṁ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavad dṛḍham | tasyāhaṁ nigrahaṁ manye vāyor iva suduṣkaram ||34||
docs.text: The mind is indeed restless, turbulent, powerful, and obstinate, O Krishna. I consider controlling it as difficult as controlling the wind.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.34

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śrī bhagavān uvāca asaṁśayam mahā-bāho manaḥ durnigraham calam abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate
śrī bhagavān uvāca | asaṁśayaṁ mahā-bāho mano durnigrahaṁ calam | abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate ||35||
docs.text: The Supreme Lord said: Undoubtedly, O mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and difficult to control. But it can be restrained by practice (abhyasa) and detachment (vairagya), O son of Kunti.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.35

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: asaṁyata-ātmanā yogaḥ duṣprāpaḥ iti me matiḥ vaśya-ātmanā tu yatatā śakyaḥ avāptum upāyataḥ
asaṁyatātmanā yogo duṣprāpa iti me matiḥ | vaśyātmanā tu yatatā śakyo 'vāptum upāyataḥ ||36||
docs.text: For one whose mind is uncontrolled, yoga is difficult to attain — this is My opinion. But for one who strives with a controlled mind, it is achievable through proper means.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.36

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: arjuna uvāca ayatiḥ śraddhayā upetaḥ yogāt calita-mānasaḥ aprāpya yoga-saṁsiddhim kām gatim kṛṣṇa gacchati
arjuna uvāca | ayatiḥ śraddhayopeto yogāc calita-mānasaḥ | aprāpya yoga-saṁsiddhiṁ kāṁ gatiṁ kṛṣṇa gacchati ||37||
docs.text: Arjuna said: What is the fate of the one who has faith but lacks sufficient effort, whose mind wanders away from yoga, and who fails to attain perfection in yoga, O Krishna?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.37

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: kaccin nobhaya-vibhraṣṭaś chinnābhram iva naśyati | apratiṣṭho mahā-bāho vimūḍho brahmaṇaḥ pathi ||38||
kaccit na ubhaya vibhraṣṭaḥ chinna-abhram iva naśyati apratiṣṭhaḥ mahā-bāho vimūḍhaḥ brahmaṇaḥ pathi
docs.text: Does such a person, fallen from both paths, not perish like a scattered cloud — without any foundation, bewildered on the path to Brahman, O mighty-armed Krishna?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.38

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: etan me saṁśayaṁ kṛṣṇa chettum arhasy aśeṣataḥ | tvad anyaḥ saṁśayasyāsya chettā na hy upapadyate ||39||
etat me saṁśayam kṛṣṇa chettum arhasi aśeṣataḥ tvat-anyaḥ saṁśayasya asya chettā na hi upapadyate
docs.text: Please dispel this doubt of mine completely, O Krishna, for no one other than You can destroy this doubt.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.39

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śrī bhagavān uvāca pārtha na eva iha na amutra vināśaḥ tasya vidyate kalyāṇa-kṛt kaścit durgatim tāta gacchati
śrī bhagavān uvāca | pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśas tasya vidyate | na hi kalyāṇa-kṛt kaścid durgatiṁ tāta gacchati ||40||
docs.text: The Supreme Lord said: O Partha, neither in this world nor in the next is there destruction for such a person. No one who does good, My dear one, ever comes to grief.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.40

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: prāpya puṇya-kṛtām lokān uṣitvā śāśvatīḥ samāḥ śucīnām śrīmatām gehe yoga-bhraṣṭaḥ abhijāyate
prāpya puṇya-kṛtāṁ lokān uṣitvā śāśvatīḥ samāḥ | śucīnāṁ śrīmatāṁ gehe yoga-bhraṣṭo 'bhijāyate ||41||
docs.text: The fallen yogi attains the higher worlds of the righteous, dwells there for many years, and is then reborn in the home of the pure and prosperous.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.41

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: athavā yoginām eva kule bhavati dhīmatām etat hi durlabhataram loke janma yat īdṛśam
athavā yoginām eva kule bhavati dhīmatām | etad dhi durlabhataraṁ loke janma yad īdṛśam ||42||
docs.text: Or the fallen yogi is born into a family of wise yogis. Such a birth is very rare indeed in this world.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.42

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: tatra tam buddhi-saṁyogam labhate paurva-dehikam yatate ca tataḥ bhūyaḥ saṁsiddhau kuru-nandana
tatra taṁ buddhi-saṁyogaṁ labhate paurva-dehikam | yatate ca tato bhūyaḥ saṁsiddhau kuru-nandana ||43||
docs.text: There, the yogi regains the spiritual consciousness from the previous life and strives once again for perfection, O joy of the Kurus.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.43

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: pūrva-abhyāsena tena eva hriyate hi avaśaḥ api saḥ jijñāsuḥ api yogasya śabda-brahma ativartate
pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva hriyate hy avaśo 'pi saḥ | jijñāsur api yogasya śabda-brahmātivartate ||44||
docs.text: By the force of previous practice alone, one is irresistibly drawn towards yoga. Even a mere inquirer of yoga transcends the ritualistic principles of the Vedas.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.44

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: prayatnād yatamānas tu yogī saṁśuddha-kilbiṣaḥ | aneka-janma-saṁsiddhas tato yāti parāṁ gatim ||45||
prayatnāt yatamānaḥ tu yogī saṁśuddha-kilbiṣaḥ aneka-janma-saṁsiddhaḥ tataḥ yāti parām gatim
docs.text: The yogi who strives with great effort, purified of all sins, perfected through many births, then attains the supreme goal.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.45

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: tapasvibhyaḥ adhikaḥ yogī jñānibhyaḥ api mataḥ adhikaḥ karmibhyaḥ ca adhikaḥ yogī tasmāt yogī bhava arjuna
tapasvibhyo 'dhiko yogī jñānibhyo 'pi mato 'dhikaḥ | karmibhyaś cādhiko yogī tasmād yogī bhavārjuna ||46||
docs.text: The yogi is greater than ascetics, greater even than the learned, and greater than those who perform rituals. Therefore, be a yogi, O Arjuna!
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.46

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yoginām api sarveṣām mat-gatena antar-ātmanā śraddhāvān bhajate yaḥ mām saḥ me yuktatamaḥ mataḥ
yoginām api sarveṣāṁ mad-gatenāntar-ātmanā | śraddhāvān bhajate yo māṁ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ ||47||
docs.text: Of all yogis, the one who worships Me with full faith, with the inner self absorbed in Me — that one is the most intimately united with Me and is the highest of all.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 6.47

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śrī bhagavān uvāca mayi āsakta-manāḥ pārtha yogam yuñjan mad-āśrayaḥ asaṁśayam samagram mām yathā jñāsyasi tat śṛṇu
śrī bhagavān uvāca | mayy āsakta-manāḥ pārtha yogaṁ yuñjan mad-āśrayaḥ | asaṁśayaṁ samagraṁ māṁ yathā jñāsyasi tac chṛṇu ||1||
docs.text: The Supreme Lord said: O Partha, hear how you shall know Me completely and without doubt, with your mind attached to Me, practicing yoga and taking refuge in Me.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.1

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: jñānam te aham sa-vijñānam idam vakṣyāmi aśeṣataḥ yat jñātvā na iha bhūyaḥ anyat jñātavyam avaśiṣyate
jñānaṁ te 'haṁ sa-vijñānam idaṁ vakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ | yaj jñātvā neha bhūyo 'nyaj jñātavyam avaśiṣyate ||2||
docs.text: I shall declare to you in full this knowledge along with realization, knowing which nothing further remains to be known in this world.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.2

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: manuṣyāṇām sahasreṣu kaścit yatati siddhaye yatatām api siddhānām kaścit mām vetti tattvataḥ
manuṣyāṇāṁ sahasreṣu kaścid yatati siddhaye | yatatām api siddhānāṁ kaścin māṁ vetti tattvataḥ ||3||
docs.text: Among thousands of human beings, hardly one strives for perfection; and among those who strive and attain perfection, hardly one knows Me in truth.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.3

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: bhūmir āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ khaṁ mano buddhir eva ca | ahaṅkāra itīyaṁ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā ||4||
bhūmiḥ āpaḥ analaḥ vāyuḥ kham manaḥ buddhiḥ eva ca ahaṅkāraḥ iti iyam me bhinnā prakṛtiḥ aṣṭadhā
docs.text: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and ego — thus is My material nature divided eightfold.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.4

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: apareyam itas tv anyāṁ prakṛtiṁ viddhi me parām | jīva-bhūtāṁ mahā-bāho yayedaṁ dhāryate jagat ||5||
aparā iyam itaḥ tu anyām prakṛtim viddhi me parām jīva-bhūtām mahā-bāho yayā idam dhāryate jagat
docs.text: This is My lower nature. But know My other, higher nature — the living consciousness, O mighty-armed one — by which this entire world is sustained.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.5

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: etad-yonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇīty upadhāraya | ahaṁ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā ||6||
etat yonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇi iti upadhāraya aham kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ tathā
docs.text: Know that all living beings have their source in these two natures. I am the origin and the dissolution of the entire universe.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.6

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: mattaḥ parataram na anyat kiñcit asti dhanañjaya mayi sarvam idam protam sūtre maṇi-gaṇāḥ iva
mattaḥ parataraṁ nānyat kiñcid asti dhanañjaya | mayi sarvam idaṁ protaṁ sūtre maṇi-gaṇā iva ||7||
docs.text: There is nothing whatsoever higher than Me, O Dhananjaya. Everything is strung upon Me, as pearls are strung on a thread.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.7

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: rasaḥ aham apsu kaunteya prabhā asmi śaśi-sūryayoḥ praṇavaḥ sarva-vedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣam nṛṣu
raso 'ham apsu kaunteya prabhāsmi śaśi-sūryayoḥ | praṇavaḥ sarva-vedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṁ nṛṣu ||8||
docs.text: I am the taste in water, O son of Kunti. I am the light in the moon and sun, the sacred syllable Om in all the Vedas, sound in ether, and ability in human beings.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.8

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: puṇyaḥ gandhaḥ pṛthivyām ca tejaḥ asmi vibhāvasau jīvanam sarva-bhūteṣu tapaḥ tapasviṣu
puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛthivyāṁ ca tejaś cāsmi vibhāvasau | jīvanaṁ sarva-bhūteṣu tapaś cāsmi tapasviṣu ||9||
docs.text: I am the pure fragrance of the earth, the brilliance in fire, the life in all beings, and the austerity of the ascetics.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.9

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: bījam mām sarva-bhūtānām viddhi pārtha sanātanam buddhiḥ buddhimatām asmi tejaḥ tejasvinām aham
bījaṁ māṁ sarva-bhūtānāṁ viddhi pārtha sanātanam | buddhir buddhimatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham ||10||
docs.text: Know Me, O Partha, as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the intelligence of the intelligent and the splendor of the splendid.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.10

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: balam balavatām ca aham kāma rāga vivarjitam dharmāviruddhaḥ bhūteṣu kāmaḥ asmi bharatarṣabha
balaṁ balavatāṁ cāhaṁ kāma-rāga-vivarjitam | dharmāviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo 'smi bharatarṣabha ||11||
docs.text: I am the strength of the strong, devoid of desire and attachment. I am the desire in beings that is not contrary to dharma, O best of the Bharatas.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.11

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: ye caiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasās tāmasāś ca ye | matta eveti tān viddhi na tv ahaṁ teṣu te mayi ||12||
ye sāttvikāḥ bhāvāḥ rājasāḥ tāmasāḥ mattaḥ eva tān viddhi na aham teṣu te mayi
docs.text: Whatever states of being there are — whether sattvic, rajasic, or tamasic — know that they all proceed from Me alone. Yet I am not in them; they are in Me.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.12

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: tribhir guṇa-mayair bhāvair ebhiḥ sarvam idaṁ jagat | mohitaṁ nābhijānāti mām ebhyaḥ param avyayam ||13||
tribhiḥ guṇa-mayaiḥ bhāvaiḥ ebhiḥ sarvam jagat mohitam na abhijānāti mām param avyayam
docs.text: Deluded by these three states composed of the gunas, this entire world does not recognize Me, who am beyond them and imperishable.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.13

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: daivī hi eṣā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā mām eva ye prapadyante māyām taranti te
daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā | mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṁ taranti te ||14||
docs.text: This divine maya of Mine, consisting of the three gunas, is very difficult to overcome. But those who surrender unto Me alone cross beyond this illusion.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.14

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: na mām duṣkṛtinaḥ mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ māyayāpahṛta-jñānāḥ āsuram bhāvam āśritāḥ
na māṁ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ | māyayāpahṛta-jñānā āsuraṁ bhāvam āśritāḥ ||15||
docs.text: The evil-doers, the foolish, the lowest of mankind, those whose knowledge is stolen by illusion, and those of demonic nature — they do not surrender unto Me.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.15

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: catur-vidhā bhajante māṁ janāḥ sukṛtino 'rjuna | ārto jijñāsur arthārthī jñānī ca bharatarṣabha ||16||
catur-vidhāḥ bhajante mām janāḥ sukṛtinaḥ ārtaḥ jijñāsuḥ arthārthī jñānī bharatarṣabha
docs.text: Four kinds of pious people worship Me, O Arjuna — the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise, O best of the Bharatas.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.16

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: teṣām jñānī nitya-yuktaḥ eka-bhaktiḥ viśiṣyate priyaḥ jñāninaḥ atyartham aham saḥ mama
teṣāṁ jñānī nitya-yukta eka-bhaktir viśiṣyate | priyo hi jñānino 'tyartham ahaṁ sa ca mama priyaḥ ||17||
docs.text: Of these, the wise one who is ever steadfast and devoted to the One alone excels. I am exceedingly dear to the wise one, and he is dear to Me.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.17

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tv ātmaiva me matam | āsthitaḥ sa hi yuktātmā mām evānuttamāṁ gatim ||18||
udārāḥ sarve eva ete jñānī tu ātmā eva me matam āsthitaḥ yuktātmā anuttamām gatim
docs.text: All these are indeed noble, but the wise one I regard as My very self. For with a steadfast mind, he is established in Me alone as the supreme goal.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.18

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: bahūnām janmanām ante jñānavān mām prapadyate vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti saḥ mahātmā su-durlabhaḥ
bahūnāṁ janmanām ante jñānavān māṁ prapadyate | vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti sa mahātmā su-durlabhaḥ ||19||
docs.text: After many births, the one possessed of wisdom surrenders unto Me, knowing 'Vasudeva is everything.' Such a great soul is very rare.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.19

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: kāmais tais tair hṛta-jñānāḥ prapadyante 'nya-devatāḥ | taṁ taṁ niyamam āsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā ||20||
kāmaiḥ taiḥ taiḥ hṛta-jñānāḥ prapadyante anya-devatāḥ tam tam niyamam āsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā
docs.text: Those whose knowledge has been carried away by various desires surrender to other deities, following various rules and rituals, driven by their own nature.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.20

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yaḥ yaḥ yām yām tanum bhaktaḥ śraddhayā arcitum icchati tasya tasya acalām śraddhām vidadhāmi aham
yo yo yāṁ yāṁ tanuṁ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitum icchati | tasya tasyācalāṁ śraddhāṁ tām eva vidadhāmy aham ||21||
docs.text: Whatever form a devotee wishes to worship with faith — I make that faith of his steady and unwavering.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.21

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: sa tayā śraddhayā yuktas tasyārādhanam īhate | labhate ca tataḥ kāmān mayaiva vihitān hi tān ||22||
saḥ tayā śraddhayā yuktaḥ tasya ārādhanam īhate labhate kāmān mayā eva vihitān hi tān
docs.text: Endowed with that faith, he worships that particular deity and obtains his desires — but those desires are actually granted by Me alone.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.22

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: antavat tu phalam teṣām tat bhavati alpa-medhasām devān deva-yajaḥ yānti mad-bhaktāḥ mām api
antavat tu phalaṁ teṣāṁ tad bhavaty alpa-medhasām | devān deva-yajo yānti mad-bhaktā yānti mām api ||23||
docs.text: But the fruit gained by those of small understanding is temporary. The worshippers of the gods go to the gods, but My devotees come to Me.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.23

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: avyaktam vyaktim āpannam manyante mām abuddhayaḥ param bhāvam ajānantaḥ avyayam anuttamam
avyaktaṁ vyaktim āpannaṁ manyante mām abuddhayaḥ | paraṁ bhāvam ajānanto mamāvyayam anuttamam ||24||
docs.text: The unintelligent think that I, the unmanifest, have taken on a manifest form. They do not know My higher nature, which is imperishable and unsurpassed.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.24

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: na aham prakāśaḥ sarvasya yoga-māyā samāvṛtaḥ mūḍhaḥ ayam lokaḥ mām ajam avyayam
nāhaṁ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yoga-māyā-samāvṛtaḥ | mūḍho 'yaṁ nābhijānāti loko mām ajam avyayam ||25||
docs.text: I am not revealed to everyone, being veiled by My yoga-maya. This deluded world does not recognize Me as the unborn and imperishable.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.25

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: veda aham samatītāni vartamānāni arjuna bhaviṣyāṇi bhūtāni mām tu veda na kaścana
vedāhaṁ samatītāni vartamānāni cārjuna | bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni māṁ tu veda na kaścana ||26||
docs.text: I know all beings of the past, present, and future, O Arjuna — but no one knows Me.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.26

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: icchā dveṣa samutthena dvandva mohena bhārata sarva-bhūtāni sammoham sarge yānti parantapa
icchā-dveṣa-samutthena dvandva-mohena bhārata | sarva-bhūtāni sammohaṁ sarge yānti parantapa ||27||
docs.text: O Bharata, all beings are born into delusion, bewildered by the dualities arising from desire and aversion, O scorcher of foes.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.27

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yeṣām tu anta-gatam pāpam janānām puṇya-karmaṇām te dvandva-moha-nirmuktāḥ bhajante mām dṛḍha-vratāḥ
yeṣāṁ tv anta-gataṁ pāpaṁ janānāṁ puṇya-karmaṇām | te dvandva-moha-nirmuktā bhajante māṁ dṛḍha-vratāḥ ||28||
docs.text: But those persons whose sins have come to an end, who act virtuously — they, freed from the delusion of opposites, worship Me with firm resolve.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.28

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: jarā maraṇa mokṣāya mām āśritya yatanti ye te brahma tat viduḥ kṛtsnam adhyātmam karma akhilam
jarā-maraṇa-mokṣāya mām āśritya yatanti ye | te brahma tad viduḥ kṛtsnam adhyātmaṁ karma cākhilam ||29||
docs.text: Those who strive for liberation from old age and death, taking refuge in Me — they come to know Brahman completely, the Self, and the entirety of karma.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.29

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: sa adhibhūta adhidaivam mām sa adhiyajñam ye viduḥ prayāṇa-kāle api ca te yukta-cetasaḥ
sādhibhūtādhidaivaṁ māṁ sādhiyajñaṁ ca ye viduḥ | prayāṇa-kāle 'pi ca māṁ te vidur yukta-cetasaḥ ||30||
docs.text: Those who know Me as the governing principle of the material realm, the divine realm, and the realm of sacrifice — they, with steadfast minds, know Me even at the time of death.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 7.30

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: arjuna uvāca kim tat brahma kim adhyātmam kim karma puruṣottama adhibhūtam ca kim proktam adhidaivam kim ucyate
arjuna uvāca | kiṁ tad brahma kim adhyātmaṁ kiṁ karma puruṣottama | adhibhūtaṁ ca kiṁ proktam adhidaivaṁ kim ucyate ||1||
docs.text: Arjuna said: What is Brahman? What is adhyatma? What is karma, O Supreme Person? What is said to be adhibhuta? And what is called adhidaiva?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.1

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: adhiyajñaḥ katham kaḥ atra dehe asmin madhusūdana prayāṇa-kāle ca katham jñeyaḥ asi niyatātmabhiḥ
adhiyajñaḥ kathaṁ ko 'tra dehe 'smin madhusūdana | prayāṇa-kāle ca kathaṁ jñeyo 'si niyatātmabhiḥ ||2||
docs.text: Who is adhiyajna and how does he dwell in this body, O Madhusudana? And how are You to be known at the time of death by those of steadfast mind?
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.2

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śrī bhagavān uvāca akṣaram brahma paramam svabhāvaḥ adhyātmam ucyate bhūta-bhāvodbhava-karaḥ visargaḥ karma-saṁjñitaḥ
śrī bhagavān uvāca | akṣaraṁ brahma paramaṁ svabhāvo 'dhyātmam ucyate | bhūta-bhāvodbhava-karo visargaḥ karma-saṁjñitaḥ ||3||
docs.text: The Supreme Lord said: Brahman is the imperishable, the Supreme. Adhyatma is one's own nature (svabhava). The creative force that brings forth the existence of beings is called karma.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.3

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: adhibhūtam kṣaraḥ bhāvaḥ puruṣaḥ ca adhidaivatam adhiyajñaḥ aham eva atra dehe deha-bhṛtām vara
adhibhūtaṁ kṣaro bhāvaḥ puruṣaś cādhidaivatam | adhiyajño 'ham evātra dehe deha-bhṛtāṁ vara ||4||
docs.text: Adhibhuta is the perishable material nature. Adhidaiva is the cosmic spirit, the Purusha. And adhiyajna is I Myself alone, here in this body, O best among the embodied.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.4

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: anta-kāle ca mām eva smaran muktvā kalevaram yaḥ prayāti saḥ mad-bhāvam yāti na asti atra saṁśayaḥ
anta-kāle ca mām eva smaran muktvā kalevaram | yaḥ prayāti sa mad-bhāvaṁ yāti nāsty atra saṁśayaḥ ||5||
docs.text: And whoever, at the time of death, remembers Me alone and departs, leaving the body — that one attains My being. There is no doubt about this.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.5

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yam yam vā api smaran bhāvam tyajati ante kalevaram tam tam eva eti kaunteya sadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ
yaṁ yaṁ vāpi smaran bhāvaṁ tyajaty ante kalevaram | taṁ tam evaiti kaunteya sadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ ||6||
docs.text: Whatever state of being one remembers when leaving the body at the end, that very state one attains, O Kaunteya, being always absorbed in that thought.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.6

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu mām anusmara yudhya ca mayi arpita-mano-buddhiḥ mām eva eṣyasi asaṁśayam
tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu mām anusmara yudhya ca | mayy arpita-mano-buddhir mām evaiṣyasy asaṁśayam ||7||
docs.text: Therefore, at all times remember Me and fight. With mind and intellect surrendered to Me, you shall surely come to Me alone — there is no doubt.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.7

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: abhyāsa-yoga-yuktena cetasā na anya-gāminā paramam puruṣam divyam yāti pārtha anucintayan
abhyāsa-yoga-yuktena cetasā nānya-gāminā | paramaṁ puruṣaṁ divyaṁ yāti pārthānucintayan ||8||
docs.text: With a mind disciplined by the practice of yoga and not wandering to anything else, one who constantly meditates on the Supreme Divine Person reaches Him, O Partha.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.8

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: kavim purāṇam anuśāsitāram aṇoḥ aṇīyāṁsam anusmaret yaḥ sarvasya dhātāram acintya-rūpam āditya-varṇam tamasaḥ parastāt
kaviṁ purāṇam anuśāsitāram aṇor aṇīyāṁsam anusmared yaḥ | sarvasya dhātāram acintya-rūpam āditya-varṇaṁ tamasaḥ parastāt ||9||
docs.text: He who meditates on the omniscient ancient seer, the ruler of all, subtler than the subtlest, the sustainer of everything, whose form is inconceivable, effulgent like the sun, beyond all darkness —
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.9

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: prayāṇa-kāle manasā acalena bhaktyā yuktaḥ yoga-balena ca eva bhruvoḥ madhye prāṇam āveśya samyak saḥ tam param puruṣam upaiti divyam
prayāṇa-kāle manasācalena bhaktyā yukto yoga-balena caiva | bhruvor madhye prāṇam āveśya samyak sa taṁ paraṁ puruṣam upaiti divyam ||10||
docs.text: At the time of death, with an unwavering mind, endowed with devotion and the power of yoga, fixing the life force completely between the eyebrows — that person reaches the Supreme Divine Person.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.10

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yad akṣaraṁ veda-vido vadanti viśanti yad yatayo vīta-rāgāḥ | yad icchanto brahmacaryaṁ caranti tat te padaṁ saṅgraheṇa pravakṣye ||11||
yat akṣaram veda-vidaḥ vadanti viśanti yat yatayaḥ vīta-rāgāḥ yat icchantaḥ brahmacaryam caranti tat te padam saṅgraheṇa pravakṣye
docs.text: That which the knowers of the Vedas call the imperishable, which the ascetics free from passion enter, and desiring which they practice brahmacharya — that goal I shall briefly declare to you.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.11

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: sarva dvārāṇi saṁyamya manaḥ hṛdi nirudhya ca mūrdhni ādhāya ātmanaḥ prāṇam āsthitaḥ yoga-dhāraṇām
sarva-dvārāṇi saṁyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca | mūrdhny ādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇam āsthito yoga-dhāraṇām ||12||
docs.text: Closing all the gates of the body, confining the mind in the heart, fixing one's life-breath in the head, established in yogic concentration —
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.12

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: oṁ iti ekākṣaram brahma vyāharan mām anusmaran yaḥ prayāti tyajan deham saḥ yāti paramām gatim
oṁ ity ekākṣaraṁ brahma vyāharan mām anusmaran | yaḥ prayāti tyajan dehaṁ sa yāti paramāṁ gatim ||13||
docs.text: Uttering the single syllable Om — which is Brahman — and remembering Me, whoever departs leaving the body, that one attains the supreme goal.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.13

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: ananya-cetāḥ satatam yaḥ mām smarati nityaśaḥ tasya aham sulabhaḥ pārtha nitya-yuktasya yoginaḥ
ananya-cetāḥ satataṁ yo māṁ smarati nityaśaḥ | tasyāhaṁ sulabhaḥ pārtha nitya-yuktasya yoginaḥ ||14||
docs.text: For one who constantly remembers Me without any other thought, O Partha — for that ever-united yogi, I am easy to attain.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.14

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: mām upetya punar janma duḥkhālayam aśāśvatam na āpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṁsiddhim paramām gatāḥ
mām upetya punar janma duḥkhālayam aśāśvatam | nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṁsiddhiṁ paramāṁ gatāḥ ||15||
docs.text: Having attained Me, the great souls do not take rebirth in this temporary world of suffering, for they have reached the highest perfection.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.15

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: ā brahma-bhuvanāt lokāḥ punar āvartinaḥ arjuna mām upetya tu kaunteya punar janma na vidyate
ā-brahma-bhuvanāl lokāḥ punar āvartino 'rjuna | mām upetya tu kaunteya punar janma na vidyate ||16||
docs.text: From the realm of Brahma downwards, all worlds are subject to return, O Arjuna. But having attained Me, O son of Kunti, there is no rebirth.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.16

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: sahasra yuga paryantam ahaḥ yat brahmaṇaḥ viduḥ rātrim yuga-sahasrāntām te aho-rātra-vidaḥ janāḥ
sahasra-yuga-paryantam ahar yad brahmaṇo viduḥ | rātriṁ yuga-sahasrāntāṁ te 'ho-rātra-vido janāḥ ||17||
docs.text: Those who know that the day of Brahma lasts a thousand yugas and the night of Brahma ends after a thousand yugas — they are the knowers of day and night.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.17

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: avyaktād vyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavanty ahar-āgame | rātry-āgame pralīyante tatraivāvyakta-saṁjñake ||18||
avyaktāt vyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavanti ahar-āgame rātry-āgame pralīyante tatra eva avyakta-saṁjñake
docs.text: From the unmanifest, all manifestations emerge at the coming of day; at the coming of night, they dissolve into that which is called the unmanifest.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.18

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: bhūta-grāmaḥ sa evāyaṁ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate | rātry-āgame 'vaśaḥ pārtha prabhavaty ahar-āgame ||19||
bhūta-grāmaḥ saḥ eva ayam bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate rātry-āgame avaśaḥ pārtha prabhavati ahar-āgame
docs.text: This same multitude of beings, coming forth again and again, dissolves helplessly at the coming of night, O Partha, and comes forth again at the coming of day.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.19

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: paras tasmāt tu bhāvo 'nyo 'vyakto 'vyaktāt sanātanaḥ | yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati ||20||
paraḥ tasmāt tu bhāvaḥ anyaḥ avyaktaḥ avyaktāt sanātanaḥ yaḥ saḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati
docs.text: But beyond this unmanifest, there is another eternal unmanifest existence — that Supreme Being who does not perish even when all beings perish.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.20

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: avyaktaḥ akṣaraḥ iti uktaḥ tam āhuḥ paramām gatim yam prāpya na nivartante tat dhāma paramam mama
avyakto 'kṣara ity uktas tam āhuḥ paramāṁ gatim | yaṁ prāpya na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṁ mama ||21||
docs.text: That which is called the Unmanifest and the Imperishable — that is said to be the highest goal. Those who attain it do not return. That is My supreme abode.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.21

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyas tv ananyayā | yasyāntaḥ-sthāni bhūtāni yena sarvam idaṁ tatam ||22||
puruṣaḥ saḥ paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyaḥ tu ananyayā yasya antaḥ-sthāni bhūtāni yena sarvam idam tatam
docs.text: That Supreme Person, O Partha, is attainable by exclusive devotion — He within whom all beings dwell, and by whom all this universe is pervaded.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.22

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yatra kāle tu anāvṛttim āvṛttim ca eva yoginaḥ prayātāḥ yānti tam kālam vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha
yatra kāle tv anāvṛttim āvṛttiṁ caiva yoginaḥ | prayātā yānti taṁ kālaṁ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha ||23||
docs.text: O best of the Bharatas, I shall now tell you of the times at which yogis departing never return, and also the times at which they depart and return.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.23

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: agnir jyotir ahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇ-māsā uttarāyaṇam | tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahma-vido janāḥ ||24||
agniḥ jyotiḥ ahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇ-māsāḥ uttarāyaṇam tatra prayātāḥ gacchanti brahma brahma-vidaḥ janāḥ
docs.text: Fire, light, daytime, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern solstice — departing by this path, the knowers of Brahman go to Brahman.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.24

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: dhūmaḥ rātriḥ tathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇ-māsāḥ dakṣiṇāyanam tatra cāndramasam jyotiḥ yogī prāpya nivartate
dhūmo rātris tathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇ-māsā dakṣiṇāyanam | tatra cāndramasaṁ jyotir yogī prāpya nivartate ||25||
docs.text: Smoke, night, the dark fortnight, the six months of the southern solstice — by this path, the yogi attains the lunar light and returns.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.25

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śukla kṛṣṇe gatī hi ete jagataḥ śāśvate mate ekayā yāti anāvṛttim anyayā āvartate punaḥ
śukla-kṛṣṇe gatī hy ete jagataḥ śāśvate mate | ekayā yāty anāvṛttim anyayāvartate punaḥ ||26||
docs.text: These two paths — the bright and the dark — are considered eternal for the world. By one, a person goes never to return; by the other, one returns again.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.26

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: na ete sṛtī pārtha jānan yogī muhyati kaścana tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu yoga-yuktaḥ bhava arjuna
naite sṛtī pārtha jānan yogī muhyati kaścana | tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu yoga-yukto bhavārjuna ||27||
docs.text: Knowing these two paths, O Partha, no yogi is deluded. Therefore, at all times, be steadfast in yoga, O Arjuna.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.27

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu ca eva dāneṣu yat puṇya-phalam pradiṣṭam atyeti tat sarvam idam viditvā yogī param sthānam upaiti ca ādyam
vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva dāneṣu yat puṇya-phalaṁ pradiṣṭam | atyeti tat sarvam idaṁ viditvā yogī paraṁ sthānam upaiti cādyam ||28||
docs.text: Whatever merit is declared in the study of the Vedas, in the performance of sacrifices, in austerities, and in charity — the yogi who knows this transcends all of it and attains the supreme, primal abode.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 8.28

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: śrī bhagavān uvāca idam tu te guhyatamam pravakṣyāmi anasūyave jñānam vijñāna-sahitam yat jñātvā mokṣyase aśubhāt
śrī bhagavān uvāca | idaṁ tu te guhyatamaṁ pravakṣyāmy anasūyave | jñānaṁ vijñāna-sahitaṁ yaj jñātvā mokṣyase 'śubhāt ||1||
docs.text: The Supreme Lord said: To you who are free from envy, I shall now declare this most secret knowledge combined with direct realization, knowing which you shall be freed from all that is inauspicious.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.1

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: rāja-vidyā rāja-guhyam pavitram idam uttamam pratyakṣa-avagamam dharmyam su-sukham kartum avyayam
rāja-vidyā rāja-guhyaṁ pavitram idam uttamam | pratyakṣāvagamaṁ dharmyaṁ su-sukhaṁ kartum avyayam ||2||
docs.text: This is the king of all knowledge, the king of all secrets, the supreme purifier, directly realizable through experience, righteous, very easy to practice, and imperishable.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.2

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya parantapa | aprāpya māṁ nivartante mṛtyu-saṁsāra-vartmani ||3||
aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣāḥ dharmasya asya parantapa aprāpya mām nivartante mṛtyu-saṁsāra-vartmani
docs.text: Those who have no faith in this dharma, O Parantapa, without attaining Me, return to the path of this mortal world of death and rebirth.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.3

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: mayā tatam idam sarvam jagat avyakta-mūrtinā mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni na ca aham teṣu avasthitaḥ
mayā tatam idaṁ sarvaṁ jagad avyakta-mūrtinā | mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni na cāhaṁ teṣv avasthitaḥ ||4||
docs.text: By Me, in My unmanifest form, this entire universe is pervaded. All beings exist in Me, but I do not dwell in them.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.4

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: na ca mat-sthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram bhūta-bhṛt bhūta-sthaḥ mama ātmā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ
na ca mat-sthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram | bhūta-bhṛn na ca bhūta-stho mamātmā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ ||5||
docs.text: And yet beings do not dwell in Me — behold My divine yoga! My Self sustains all beings but does not dwell in them; My Self is the very source of all beings.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.5

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yathā ākāśa-sthitaḥ nityam vāyuḥ sarvatra-gaḥ mahān tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni mat-sthāni iti upadhāraya
yathākāśa-sthito nityaṁ vāyuḥ sarvatra-go mahān | tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni mat-sthānīty upadhāraya ||6||
docs.text: As the mighty wind, blowing everywhere, always rests in space, know that in the same way, all beings rest in Me.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.6

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: sarva-bhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtim yānti māmikām kalpa-kṣaye punaḥ tāni kalpādau visṛjāmi aham
sarva-bhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtiṁ yānti māmikām | kalpa-kṣaye punas tāni kalpādau visṛjāmy aham ||7||
docs.text: All beings, O Kaunteya, enter into My prakriti at the end of a kalpa. At the beginning of the next kalpa, I send them forth again.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.7

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: prakṛtim svām avaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ bhūta-grāmam imam kṛtsnam avaśam prakṛteḥ vaśāt
prakṛtiṁ svām avaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ | bhūta-grāmam imaṁ kṛtsnam avaśaṁ prakṛter vaśāt ||8||
docs.text: Resorting to My own prakriti, I send forth again and again this entire multitude of beings, who are helpless under the sway of prakriti.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.8

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: na ca mām tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya udāsīnavat āsīnam asaktam teṣu karmasu
na ca māṁ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya | udāsīnavad āsīnam asaktaṁ teṣu karmasu ||9||
docs.text: These actions do not bind Me, O Dhananjaya. I sit as if indifferent, unattached to those actions.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.9

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: mayā adhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sa-cara-acaram hetunā anena kaunteya jagat viparivartate
mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sa-carācaram | hetunānena kaunteya jagad viparivartate ||10||
docs.text: Under My supervision, prakriti produces the moving and the unmoving. By this cause, O Kaunteya, the world revolves.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.10

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: avajānanti mām mūḍhāḥ mānuṣīm tanum āśritam param bhāvam ajānantaḥ mama bhūta-maheśvaram
avajānanti māṁ mūḍhā mānuṣīṁ tanum āśritam | paraṁ bhāvam ajānanto mama bhūta-maheśvaram ||11||
docs.text: Fools disregard Me when I take a human form, not knowing My higher nature as the great Lord of all beings.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.11

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: moghāśā mogha-karmāṇo mogha-jñānā vicetasaḥ | rākṣasīm āsurīṁ caiva prakṛtiṁ mohinīṁ śritāḥ ||12||
moghāśāḥ mogha-karmāṇaḥ mogha-jñānāḥ vicetasaḥ rākṣasīm āsurīm ca eva prakṛtim mohinīm śritāḥ
docs.text: Of vain hopes, vain actions, vain knowledge, and senseless, they partake of the deluding nature of rakshasas and asuras.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.12

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: mahātmānas tu māṁ pārtha daivīṁ prakṛtim āśritāḥ | bhajanty ananya-manaso jñātvā bhūtādim avyayam ||13||
mahātmānaḥ tu mām pārtha daivīm prakṛtim āśritāḥ bhajanti ananya-manasaḥ jñātvā bhūtādim avyayam
docs.text: But the great souls, O Partha, partaking of the divine nature, worship Me with a single mind, knowing Me as the imperishable source of all beings.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.13

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: satatam kīrtayantaḥ mām yatantaḥ ca dṛḍha-vratāḥ namasyantaḥ bhaktyā nitya-yuktāḥ upāsate
satataṁ kīrtayanto māṁ yatantaś ca dṛḍha-vratāḥ | namasyantaś ca māṁ bhaktyā nitya-yuktā upāsate ||14||
docs.text: Always glorifying Me, striving with firm resolve, bowing down to Me with devotion, always united with Me, they worship Me.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.14

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: jñāna-yajñena ca api anye yajantaḥ mām upāsate ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvato-mukham
jñāna-yajñena cāpy anye yajanto mām upāsate | ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvato-mukham ||15||
docs.text: Others, offering the sacrifice of knowledge, worship Me as the One, as the distinct, and in My universal form facing everywhere.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.15

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: aham kratuḥ yajñaḥ svadhā auṣadham mantraḥ ājyam agniḥ hutam
ahaṁ kratur ahaṁ yajñaḥ svadhāham aham auṣadham | mantro 'ham aham evājyam aham agnir ahaṁ hutam ||16||
docs.text: I am the ritual, I am the sacrifice, I am the offering to ancestors, I am the herb. I am the mantra, I am the ghee, I am the fire, and I am the act of offering.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.16

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: pitā aham asya jagataḥ mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ vedyam pavitram oṁkāraḥ ṛk sāma yajuḥ
pitāham asya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ | vedyaṁ pavitram oṁkāra ṛk sāma yajur eva ca ||17||
docs.text: I am the father of this universe, the mother, the sustainer, the grandsire. I am the object of knowledge, the purifier, the syllable Om, and also the Rig, Sama, and Yajur Vedas.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.17

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: gatir bhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇaṁ suhṛt | prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānaṁ nidhānaṁ bījam avyayam ||18||
gatiḥ bhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇam suhṛt prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānam nidhānam bījam avyayam
docs.text: I am the goal, the sustainer, the master, the witness, the abode, the shelter, the friend. I am the origin, dissolution, foundation, resting place, and the imperishable seed.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.18

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: tapāmi aham varṣam nigṛhṇāmi utsṛjāmi ca amṛtam mṛtyuḥ sat asat arjuna
tapāmy aham ahaṁ varṣaṁ nigṛhṇāmy utsṛjāmi ca | amṛtaṁ caiva mṛtyuś ca sad asac cāham arjuna ||19||
docs.text: I give heat; I withhold and send forth rain. I am immortality and also death. I am being and non-being, O Arjuna.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.19

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: trai-vidyā māṁ soma-pāḥ pūta-pāpā yajñair iṣṭvā svar-gatiṁ prārthayante | te puṇyam āsādya surendra-lokam aśnanti divyān divi deva-bhogān ||20||
trai-vidyāḥ mām soma-pāḥ pūta-pāpāḥ yajñaiḥ iṣṭvā svar-gatim prārthayante te puṇyam āsādya surendra-lokam aśnanti divyān deva-bhogān
docs.text: The knowers of the three Vedas, who drink the soma and are purified of sin, worshipping Me with sacrifices, pray for passage to heaven. They reach the holy world of Indra and enjoy celestial pleasures of the gods.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.20

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: te tam bhuktvā svarga-lokam viśālam kṣīṇe puṇye martya-lokam viśanti evam trayī-dharmam anuprapannāḥ gatāgatam kāma-kāmāḥ labhante
te taṁ bhuktvā svarga-lokaṁ viśālaṁ kṣīṇe puṇye martya-lokaṁ viśanti | evaṁ trayī-dharmam anuprapannā gatāgataṁ kāma-kāmā labhante ||21||
docs.text: Having enjoyed the vast heavenly world, when their merit is exhausted, they return to the mortal world. Thus, following the Vedic rituals and desiring pleasures, they obtain only what comes and goes.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.21

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: ananyāś cintayanto māṁ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṁ nityābhiyuktānāṁ yoga-kṣemaṁ vahāmy aham ||22||
ananyāḥ cintayantaḥ mām ye janāḥ paryupāsate teṣām nityābhiyuktānām yoga-kṣemam vahāmi aham
docs.text: Those who worship Me alone, thinking of no other, to those ever-united devotees, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.22

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: ye 'py anya-devatā-bhaktā yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ | te 'pi mām eva kaunteya yajanty avidhi-pūrvakam ||23||
ye api anya-devatā-bhaktāḥ yajante śraddhayā anvitāḥ te api mām eva kaunteya yajanti avidhi-pūrvakam
docs.text: Even those who are devotees of other gods and worship them with faith — they too worship Me alone, O son of Kunti, though in a wrong way.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.23

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: aham hi sarva-yajñānām bhoktā ca prabhuḥ eva na tu mām abhijānanti tattvena ataḥ cyavanti te
ahaṁ hi sarva-yajñānāṁ bhoktā ca prabhur eva ca | na tu mām abhijānanti tattvenātaś cyavanti te ||24||
docs.text: I am indeed the enjoyer and the Lord of all sacrifices. But they do not know Me in truth, and therefore they fall.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.24

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yānti deva-vratā devān pitṝn yānti pitṛ-vratāḥ | bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā yānti mad-yājino 'pi mām ||25||
yānti deva-vratāḥ devān pitṝn pitṛ-vratāḥ bhūtāni bhūtejyāḥ mad-yājinaḥ api mām
docs.text: Worshippers of the devas go to the devas; worshippers of the ancestors go to the ancestors; worshippers of the spirits go to the spirits; but My worshippers come to Me.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.25

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: patram puṣpam phalam toyam yaḥ me bhaktyā prayacchati tat aham bhakti-upahṛtam aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ
patraṁ puṣpaṁ phalaṁ toyaṁ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati | tad ahaṁ bhakty-upahṛtam aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ ||26||
docs.text: Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water — that offering of love from a pure-hearted person, I accept.
docs.title: Bhagavad Gita 9.26

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Bhagavad Gita
tags: yat karoṣi yad aśnāsi yaj juhoṣi dadāsi yat | yat tapasyasi kaunteya tat kuruṣva mad-arpaṇam ||27||
yat karoṣi yat aśnāsi yat juhoṣi dadāsi yat tapasyasi kaunteya tat kuruṣva mad-arpaṇam
docs.text: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice, whatever you give, whatever austerity you practice — do it as an offering to Me, O son of Kunti.
