tags: विषयश्च महाभाग याति चैवं पृथक् पृथक्। दिवान्धाः प्राणिनः केचिद्रात्रावन्धास्तथापरे॥
docs.text: And the world of objects, blessed one, reaches each creature in its own way. Some creatures are blind by day, others blind by night,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.48

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: केचिद्दिवा तथा रात्रौ प्राणिनस्तुल्यदृष्टयः। ज्ञानिनो मनुजाः सत्यं किं तु ते न हि केवलम्॥
docs.text: and some see alike by day and by night. Human beings have knowledge, it is true — but they are not alone in having it.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.49

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: यतो हि ज्ञानिनः सर्वे पशुपक्षिमृगादयः। ज्ञानं च तन्मनुष्याणां यत्तेषां मृगपक्षिणाम्॥
docs.text: for every creature — cattle, birds, wild beasts and the rest — has knowledge. And the knowledge men have is the same as that of beasts and birds,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.50

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: मनुष्याणां च यत्तेषां तुल्यमन्यत्तथोभयोः। ज्ञानेऽपि सति पश्यैतान् पतङ्गाञ्छावचञ्चुषु॥
docs.text: and what men have, they have; in all else, too, the two are alike. Yet, for all their knowledge, look at these birds — into the beaks of their young
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.51

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: कणमोक्षादृतान्मोहात् पीड्यमानानपि क्षुधा। मानुषा मनुजव्याघ्र साभिलाषाः सुतान् प्रति॥
docs.text: they drop grain into them out of sheer delusion, though racked by hunger themselves. Men, tiger among men, long for sons
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.52

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: लोभात्प्रत्युपकाराय नन्वेतान् किं न पश्यसि। तथापि ममतावर्त्ते मोहगर्ते निपातिताः॥
docs.text: out of greed, hoping to be repaid. Do you not see them? And still they are thrown into the whirlpool of ‘mine’, into the pit of delusion —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.53

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: महामायाप्रभावेण संसारस्थितिकारिणा। तन्नात्र विस्मयः कार्यो योगनिद्रा जगत्पतेः॥
docs.text: It is the power of Mahāmāyā, who keeps the round of worldly existence turning, that casts them down. So there is nothing to wonder at here. She who is the yogic sleep of the Lord of the world —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.54

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: महामाया हरेश्चैषा तया सम्मोह्यते जगत्। ज्ञानिनामपि चेतांसि देवी भगवती हि सा॥
docs.text: — she is Hari’s Great Māyā, and by her the whole world is held in delusion. Even the minds of the wise — for she is the Goddess, the Blessed Lady —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.55

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: बलादाकृष्य मोहाय महामाया प्रयच्छति। तया विसृज्यते विश्वं जगदेतच्चराचरम्॥
docs.text: — Mahāmāyā seizes them by force and gives them over to delusion. It is she who brings forth this whole world of the moving and the still.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.56

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सैषा प्रसन्ना वरदा नृणां भवति मुक्तये। सा विद्या परमा मुक्तेर्हेतुभूता सनातनी॥
docs.text: And when she is pleased, this same Goddess grants human beings the boon of liberation. She is the supreme knowledge, the eternal cause of freedom —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.57

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: संसारबन्धहेतुश्च सैव सर्वेश्वरेश्वरी॥
docs.text: and the cause of bondage to worldly existence. She alone is sovereign over all who rule.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.58

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: भगवन् का हि सा देवी महामायेति यां भवान्॥
docs.text: Revered sir, who is this Goddess whom you call Mahāmāyā?
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.60

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ब्रवीति कथमुत्पन्ना सा कर्मास्याश्च किं द्विज। यत्प्रभावा च सा देवी यत्स्वरूपा यदुद्भवा॥
docs.text: How did she come to be, O brāhmaṇa, and what are her deeds? What is her power, what her true nature, and from where does she arise?
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.61

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तत्सर्वं श्रोतुमिच्छामि त्वत्तो ब्रह्मविदां वर॥
docs.text: All this I long to hear from you, O best of those who know Brahman.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.62

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: नित्यैव सा जगन्मूर्तिस्तया सर्वमिदं ततम्॥
docs.text: She is eternal; the world is her very form, and by her all this is pervaded.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.64

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तथापि तत्समुत्पत्तिर्बहुधा श्रूयतां मम। देवानां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थमाविर्भवति सा यदा॥
docs.text: Even so, hear from me how she comes forth, again and again. When she becomes manifest to accomplish the purpose of the gods,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.65

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: उत्पन्नेति तदा लोके सा नित्याप्यभिधीयते। योगनिद्रां यदा विष्णुर्जगत्येकार्णवीकृते॥
docs.text: then, though eternal, she is said in the world to be ‘born’. At the end of an age, when the world had become a single ocean and Viṣṇu entered his yogic sleep,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.66

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: आस्तीर्य शेषमभजत्कल्पान्ते भगवान् प्रभुः। तदा द्वावसुरौ घोरौ विख्यातौ मधुकैटभौ॥
docs.text: spreading out the serpent Śeṣa as his couch — then two dreadful asuras, the notorious Madhu and Kaiṭabha,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.67

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: विष्णुकर्णमलोद्भूतौ हन्तुं ब्रह्माणमुद्यतौ। स नाभिकमले विष्णोः स्थितो ब्रह्मा प्रजापतिः॥
docs.text: born from the wax of Viṣṇu’s ears, rose up to kill Brahmā. Brahmā, lord of creatures, seated on the lotus springing from Viṣṇu’s navel,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.68

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: दृष्ट्वा तावसुरौ चोग्रौ प्रसुप्तं च जनार्दनम्। तुष्टाव योगनिद्रां तामेकाग्रहृदयस्थितः॥
docs.text: seeing the two fierce asuras and Janārdana deep in sleep, with his heart wholly gathered, began to praise Yoganidrā —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.69

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: विबोधनार्थाय हरेर्हरिनेत्रकृतालयाम्। विश्वेश्वरीं जगद्धात्रीं स्थितिसंहारकारिणीम्॥
docs.text: to wake Hari: she who dwelt in Hari’s eyes, sovereign of the universe, sustainer of the world, who preserves it and dissolves it —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.70

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: निद्रां भगवतीं विष्णोरतुलां तेजसः प्रभुः॥
docs.text: the incomparable Lady, the Sleep of Viṣṇu. So Brahmā, lord of splendour, praised her.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.71

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: त्वं स्वाहा त्वं स्वधा त्वं हि वषट्कारः स्वरात्मिका॥
docs.text: You are Svāhā, you are Svadhā; you are the sacred cry Vaṣaṭ — your very self is the sound of the Veda.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.73

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सुधा त्वमक्षरे नित्ये त्रिधा मात्रात्मिका स्थिता। अर्धमात्रास्थिता नित्या यानुच्चार्या विशेषतः॥
docs.text: You are the nectar of immortality. In the eternal, imperishable syllable you dwell as its three sounds; and you dwell in the half-measure beyond them, eternal, which no voice can utter as a separate sound.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.74

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: त्वमेव संध्या सावित्री त्वं देवि जननी परा। त्वयैतद्धार्यते विश्वं त्वयैतत्सृज्यते जगत्॥
docs.text: You alone are the sacred twilight and the Sāvitrī verse; you, O Goddess, are the supreme Mother. By you this universe is sustained, and by you this world is brought forth.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.75

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: त्वयैतत्पाल्यते देवि त्वमत्स्यन्ते च सर्वदा। विसृष्टौ सृष्टिरूपा त्वं स्थितिरूपा च पालने॥
docs.text: By you, O Goddess, it is protected, and at the end of every age you consume it. When the world is brought forth, you are its creation; while it is sustained, you are its preservation;
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.76

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तथा संहृतिरूपान्ते जगतोऽस्य जगन्मये। महाविद्या महामाया महामेधा महास्मृतिः॥
docs.text: and at the end of this world, O you whose being is the world, you are its dissolution. You are the Great Knowledge and the Great Illusion, the Great Intelligence and the Great Memory,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.77

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: महामोहा च भवती महादेवी महासुरी। प्रकृतिस्त्वं च सर्वस्य गुणत्रयविभाविनी॥
docs.text: and Great Delusion, Great Goddess and mighty Asurī. You are the primal Nature of all things, unfolding the three qualities.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.78

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: कालरात्रिर्महारात्रिर्मोहरात्रिश्च दारुणा। त्वं श्रीस्त्वमीश्वरी त्वं ह्रीस्त्वं बुद्धिर्बोधलक्षणा॥
docs.text: You are the Night of Time, the Great Night, the terrible Night of Delusion. You are Fortune, you are the Sovereign, you are Modesty, you are Understanding, whose very mark is awakening.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.79

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: लज्जा पुष्टिस्तथा तुष्टिस्त्वं शान्तिः क्षान्तिरेव च। खड्गिनी शूलिनी घोरा गदिनी चक्रिणी तथा॥
docs.text: You are modesty, nourishment and contentment; you are peace, and patience too. You bear the sword and the trident; you are terrible; you carry the mace and the discus;
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.80

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: शङ्खिनी चापिनी बाणभुशुण्डीपरिघायुधा। सौम्या सौम्यतराशेषसौम्येभ्यस्त्वतिसुन्दरी॥
docs.text: you bear the conch and the bow, and your weapons are arrows, the bhuśuṇḍī and the iron club. Yet you are gentle — gentler than every gentle thing — and beautiful beyond measure.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.81

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: परापराणां परमा त्वमेव परमेश्वरी। यच्च किंचित्क्वचिद्वस्तु सदसद्वाखिलात्मिके॥
docs.text: Highest of all things high and low, you alone are the supreme Sovereign. And whatever thing there is, anywhere, whether it is or is not, O Soul of all —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.82

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तस्य सर्वस्य या शक्तिः सा त्वं किं स्तूयसे तदा। यया त्वया जगत्स्रष्टा जगत्पात्यत्ति यो जगत्॥
docs.text: of all that, you are the power. How then can anyone praise you? You, by whom he who creates the world, sustains the world and devours the world
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.83

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सोऽपि निद्रावशं नीतः कस्त्वां स्तोतुमिहेश्वरः। विष्णुः शरीरग्रहणमहमीशान एव च॥
docs.text: — even he has been brought under the sway of sleep. Who here has the power to praise you? Viṣṇu, I myself and Īśāna
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.84

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: कारितास्ते यतोऽतस्त्वां कः स्तोतुं शक्तिमान् भवेत्। सा त्वमित्थं प्रभावैः स्वैरुदारैर्देवि संस्तुता॥
docs.text: have been made by you to take on bodily form — so who could have the power to praise you? O Devī, praised in this way for your own exalted powers,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.85

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: मोहयैतौ दुराधर्षावसुरौ मधुकैटभौ। प्रबोधं च जगत्स्वामी नीयतामच्युतो लघु॥
docs.text: bewilder these two invincible asuras, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, and let Acyuta, the lord of the world, be woken quickly,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.86

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: बोधश्च क्रियतामस्य हन्तुमेतौ महासुरौ॥
docs.text: and let him be roused to slay these two great asuras.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.87

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: एवं स्तुता तदा देवी तामसी तत्र वेधसा॥
docs.text: Praised in this way by Brahmā, the Ordainer, the Goddess who is the dark power of sleep
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.89

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: विष्णोः प्रबोधनार्थाय निहन्तुं मधुकैटभौ। नेत्रास्यनासिकाबाहुहृदयेभ्यस्तथोरसः॥
docs.text: so that Viṣṇu might wake and slay Madhu and Kaiṭabha, came forth from his eyes, mouth, nose, arms and heart, and from his breast,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.90

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: निर्गम्य दर्शने तस्थौ ब्रह्मणोऽव्यक्तजन्मनः। उत्तस्थौ च जगन्नाथस्तया मुक्तो जनार्दनः॥
docs.text: and stood before the eyes of Brahmā, whose birth is beyond knowing. Released by her, Janārdana, lord of the world, rose
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.91

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: एकार्णवेऽहिशयनात्ततः स ददृशे च तौ। मधुकैटभौ दुरात्मानावतिवीर्यपराक्रमौ॥
docs.text: from his serpent couch on the one ocean. Then he saw the two, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, evil-hearted and of surpassing strength and prowess,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.92

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: क्रोधरक्तेक्षणावत्तुं ब्रह्माणं जनितोद्यमौ। समुत्थाय ततस्ताभ्यां युयुधे भगवान् हरिः॥
docs.text: their eyes red with rage, bent on devouring Brahmā. Rising up, the Lord Hari then fought with them
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.93

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि बाहुप्रहरणो विभुः। तावप्यतिबलोन्मत्तौ महामायाविमोहितौ॥
docs.text: for five thousand years, the all-pervading Lord fighting with his bare arms. Then the two, drunk with their own great strength and deluded by Mahāmāyā,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.94

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: उक्तवन्तौ वरोऽस्मत्तो व्रियतामिति केशवम्॥
docs.text: said to Keśava, “Choose a boon from us.”
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.95

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: भवेतामद्य मे तुष्टौ मम वध्यावुभावपि॥
docs.text: If you are pleased with me, then let both of you be slain by me today.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.97

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: किमन्येन वरेणात्र एतावद्धि वृतं मम॥
docs.text: What need have I of any other boon? This alone is my choice.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.98

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: वञ्चिताभ्यामिति तदा सर्वमापोमयं जगत्॥
docs.text: Thus deceived, the two then looked and saw the whole world turned to water,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.100

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: विलोक्य ताभ्यां गदितो भगवान् कमलेक्षणः। आवां जहि न यत्रोर्वी सलिलेन परिप्लुता॥
docs.text: and they said to the lotus-eyed Lord, “Slay us where the earth is not flooded with water.”
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.101

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तथेत्युक्त्वा भगवता शङ्खचक्रगदाभृता। कृत्वा चक्रेण वै च्छिन्ने जघने शिरसी तयोः॥
docs.text: Saying “So be it,” the Lord who bears the conch, the discus and the mace laid them on his lap and cut off their two heads with his discus.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.103

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: एवमेषा समुत्पन्ना ब्रह्मणा संस्तुता स्वयम्। प्रभावमस्या देव्यास्तु भूयः शृणु वदामि ते॥
docs.text: So it was that she appeared, praised by Brahmā himself. Now hear more of this Goddess’s power; I shall tell you.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 1.104

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: देवासुरमभूद्युद्धं पूर्णमब्दशतं पुरा। महिषेऽसुराणामधिपे देवानां च पुरन्दरे॥
docs.text: Long ago the gods and the asuras fought for a full hundred years, when Mahiṣa was lord of the asuras and Indra lord of the gods.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.2

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तत्रासुरैर्महावीर्यैर्देवसैन्यं पराजितम्। जित्वा च सकलान् देवानिन्द्रोऽभून्महिषासुरः॥
docs.text: In that war the mighty asuras routed the army of the gods; and having conquered every god, Mahiṣāsura made himself Indra.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.3

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ततः पराजिता देवाः पद्मयोनिं प्रजापतिम्। पुरस्कृत्य गतास्तत्र यत्रेशगरुडध्वजौ॥
docs.text: Then the defeated gods, with Brahmā the lotus-born creator at their head, went to where Śiva and Viṣṇu were.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.4

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: यथावृत्तं तयोस्तद्वन्महिषासुरचेष्टितम्। त्रिदशाः कथयामासुर्देवाभिभवविस्तरम्॥
docs.text: The gods told the two of them everything Mahiṣāsura had done, exactly as it happened, and the whole story of their own defeat.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.5

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सूर्येन्द्राग्न्यनिलेन्दूनां यमस्य वरुणस्य च। अन्येषां चाधिकारान् स स्वयमेवाधितिष्ठति॥
docs.text: He has seized for himself the offices of the Sun, Indra, Fire, Wind and Moon, of Yama and Varuṇa, and of the other gods besides.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.6

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: स्वर्गान्निराकृताः सर्वे तेन देवगणा भुवि। विचरन्ति यथा मर्त्या महिषेण दुरात्मना॥
docs.text: Cast out of heaven by that wicked Mahiṣa, all the gods now wander the earth like mortal men.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.7

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: एतद्वः कथितं सर्वममरारिविचेष्टितम्। शरणं वः प्रपन्नाः स्मो वधस्तस्य विचिन्त्यताम्॥
docs.text: We have told you all that the enemy of the gods has done. We have come to you for refuge: find a way to destroy him.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.8

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: इत्थं निशम्य देवानां वचांसि मधुसूदनः। चकार कोपं शम्भुश्च भ्रुकुटीकुटिलाननौ॥
docs.text: Hearing the gods speak in this way, Viṣṇu and Śiva grew angry, their faces dark with frowning brows.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.9

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ततोऽतिकोपपूर्णस्य चक्रिणो वदनात्ततः। निश्चक्राम महत्तेजो ब्रह्मणः शंकरस्य च॥
docs.text: Then from the face of Viṣṇu, the bearer of the discus, burning with anger, a great radiance came forth, and from the faces of Brahmā and Śiva as well.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.10

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अन्येषां चैव देवानां शक्रादीनां शरीरतः। निर्गतं सुमहत्तेजस्तच्चैक्यं समगच्छत॥
docs.text: From the bodies of the other gods as well, Indra and the rest, a great radiance poured forth, and all of it came together and became one.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.11

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अतीव तेजसः कूटं ज्वलन्तमिव पर्वतम्। ददृशुस्ते सुरास्तत्र ज्वालाव्याप्तदिगन्तरम्॥
docs.text: There the gods saw a vast mass of light like a mountain on fire, its flames filling every direction.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.12

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अतुलं तत्र तत्तेजः सर्वदेवशरीरजम्। एकस्थं तदभून्नारी व्याप्तलोकत्रयं त्विषा॥
docs.text: There that matchless radiance, born from the bodies of all the gods, gathered into one place and, filling the three worlds with its light, became a woman.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.13

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: यदभूच्छाम्भवं तेजस्तेनाजायत तन्मुखम्। याम्येन चाभवन् केशा बाहवो विष्णुतेजसा॥
docs.text: From Śiva’s radiance her face was formed; from Yama’s, her hair; from Viṣṇu’s, her arms.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.14

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सौम्येन स्तनयोर्युग्मं मध्यं चैन्द्रेण चाभवत्। वारुणेन च जङ्घोरू नितम्बस्तेजसा भुवः॥
docs.text: From the Moon’s radiance her breasts were formed, from Indra’s her waist, from Varuṇa’s her legs, and from the Earth’s radiance her hips.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.15

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ब्रह्मणस्तेजसा पादौ तदङ्गुल्योऽर्कतेजसा। वसूनां च कराङ्गुल्यः कौबेरेण च नासिका॥
docs.text: From Brahmā’s radiance came her feet, from the Sun’s her toes, from the Vasus’ her fingers, and from Kubera’s her nose.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.16

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तस्यास्तु दन्ताः सम्भूताः प्राजापत्येन तेजसा। नयनत्रितयं जज्ञे तथा पावकतेजसा॥
docs.text: Her teeth were formed from the radiance of Prajāpati, and her three eyes, likewise, from the radiance of Fire.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.17

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: भ्रुवौ च संध्ययोस्तेजः श्रवणावनिलस्य च। अन्येषां चैव देवानां सम्भवस्तेजसां शिवा॥
docs.text: Her brows were the radiance of the two Twilights, her ears that of the Wind; and so the auspicious Goddess arose from the radiance of all the other gods as well.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.18

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ततः समस्तदेवानां तेजोराशिसमुद्भवाम्। तां विलोक्य मुदं प्रापुरमरा महिषार्दिताः॥
docs.text: Then the gods, so long oppressed by Mahiṣa, looked on her who had arisen from the gathered radiance of them all, and they were filled with joy.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.19

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: शूलं शूलाद्विनिष्कृष्य ददौ तस्यै पिनाकधृक्। चक्रं च दत्तवान् कृष्णः समुत्पाद्य स्वचक्रतः॥
docs.text: Śiva, bearer of the Pināka bow, drew a trident out of his own trident and gave it to her; and Viṣṇu brought forth a discus from his own discus and gave it to her.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.20

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: शङ्खं च वरुणः शक्तिं ददौ तस्यै हुताशनः। मारुतो दत्तवांश्चापं बाणपूर्णे तथेषुधी॥
docs.text: Varuṇa gave her a conch, and Fire a spear; the Wind gave her a bow and two quivers full of arrows.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.21

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: वज्रमिन्द्रः समुत्पाद्य कुलिशादमराधिपः। ददौ तस्यै सहस्राक्षो घण्टामैरावताद् गजात्॥
docs.text: Indra, the thousand-eyed lord of the gods, brought forth a thunderbolt from his own and gave it to her, together with a bell from his elephant Airāvata.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.22

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: कालदण्डाद्यमो दण्डं पाशं चाम्बुपतिर्ददौ। प्रजापतिश्चाक्षमालां ददौ ब्रह्मा कमण्डलुम्॥
docs.text: Yama gave her a staff drawn from his own staff of death, and Varuṇa, lord of the waters, a noose; Prajāpati gave her a rosary, and Brahmā a water-pot.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.23

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: समस्तरोमकूपेषु निजरश्मीन् दिवाकरः। कालश्च दत्तवान् खड्गं तस्याश्चर्म च निर्मलम्॥
docs.text: The Sun filled every pore of her body with his own rays, and Time gave her a sword and a gleaming shield.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.24

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: क्षीरोदश्चामलं हारमजरे च तथाम्बरे। चूडामणिं तथा दिव्यं कुण्डले कटकानि च॥
docs.text: The Ocean of Milk gave her a spotless necklace, a pair of garments that never wear out, a heavenly crest-jewel, earrings and bracelets,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.25

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अर्धचन्द्रं तथा शुभ्रं केयूरान् सर्वबाहुषु। नूपुरौ विमलौ तद्वद् ग्रैवेयकमनुत्तमम्॥
docs.text: a gleaming crescent, armlets for all her arms, a pair of shining anklets and a peerless collar,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.26

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अङ्गुलीयकरत्नानि समस्तास्वङ्गुलीषु च। विश्वकर्मा ददौ तस्यै परशुं चातिनिर्मलम्॥
docs.text: and the finest rings for every finger. Viśvakarman gave her a gleaming axe,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.27

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अस्त्राण्यनेकरूपाणि तथाभेद्यं च दंशनम्। अम्लानपङ्कजां मालां शिरस्युरसि चापराम्॥
docs.text: missiles of many kinds and armour that nothing can pierce. A garland of unfading lotuses for her head and another for her breast
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.28

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अददज्जलधिस्तस्यै पङ्कजं चातिशोभनम्। हिमवान् वाहनं सिंहं रत्नानि विविधानि च॥
docs.text: the Ocean gave her, with a lotus of surpassing beauty. Himavat gave her a lion to ride, and jewels of every kind.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.29

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ददावशून्यं सुरया पानपात्रं धनाधिपः। शेषश्च सर्वनागेशो महामणिविभूषितम्॥
docs.text: Kubera, Lord of Wealth, gave her a drinking-cup never empty of wine; and Śeṣa, king of all serpents, a jewel-studded
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.30

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: नागहारं ददौ तस्यै धत्ते यः पृथिवीमिमाम्। अन्यैरपि सुरैर्देवी भूषणैरायुधैस्तथा॥
docs.text: serpent-necklace — Śeṣa, who bears this earth. And the Goddess, honoured by the other gods as well with ornaments and weapons,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.31

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सम्मानिता ननादोच्चैः साट्टहासं मुहुर्मुहुः। तस्या नादेन घोरेण कृत्स्नमापूरितं नभः॥
docs.text: roared aloud again and again, with peals of laughter. The whole sky was filled with her terrible roar.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.32

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अमायतातिमहता प्रतिशब्दो महानभूत् । चुक्षुभुः सकला लोकाः समुद्राश्च चकम्पिरे॥
docs.text: From that boundless, immense roar a mighty echo rang out; all the worlds were shaken and the oceans trembled.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.33

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: चचाल वसुधा चेलुः सकलाश्च महीधराः। जयेति देवाश्च मुदा तामूचुः सिंहवाहिनीम्॥
docs.text: The earth shook and all the mountains quaked, and the gods cried out in joy to the lion-rider, ‘Victory to you!’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.34

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तुष्टुवुर्मुनयश्चैनां भक्तिनम्रात्ममूर्तयः। दृष्ट्वा समस्तं संक्षुब्धं त्रैलोक्यममरारयः॥
docs.text: The sages, bowing low in devotion, sang her praise. But the enemies of the gods, seeing the three worlds in turmoil,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.35

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सन्नद्धाखिलसैन्यास्ते समुत्तस्थुरुदायुधाः। आः किमेतदिति क्रोधादाभाष्य महिषासुरः॥
docs.text: rose up, weapons raised, their whole army in arms. ‘Ha! What is this?’ cried Mahiṣāsura in fury,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.36

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अभ्यधावत तं शब्दमशेषैरसुरैर्वृतः। स ददर्श ततो देवीं व्याप्तलोकत्रयां त्विषा॥
docs.text: and charged towards the sound with all his asuras around him. Then he saw the Goddess, her radiance filling the three worlds,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.37

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: पादाक्रान्त्या नतभुवं किरीटोल्लिखिताम्बराम्। क्षोभिताशेषपातालां धनुर्ज्यानिःस्वनेन ताम्॥
docs.text: the earth bending beneath her tread, her crown grazing the sky, the twang of her bowstring shaking the underworlds to their depths,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.38

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: दिशो भुजसहस्रेण समन्ताद् व्याप्य संस्थिताम्। ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तया देव्या सुरद्विषाम्॥
docs.text: standing with her thousand arms spread through every quarter. Then the battle began between the Goddess and the enemies of the gods,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.39

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: शस्त्रास्त्रैर्बहुधा मुक्तैरादीपितदिगन्तरम्। महिषासुरसेनानीश्चिक्षुराख्यो महासुरः॥
docs.text: a battle in which the weapons and missiles they hurled set the whole horizon ablaze. Cikṣura, the mighty asura, Mahiṣāsura’s commander,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.40

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: युयुधे चामरश्चान्यैश्चतुरङ्गबलान्वितः। रथानामयुतैः षड्भिरुदग्राख्यो महासुरः॥
docs.text: joined battle; so did Cāmara, with others and an army of all four arms. Udagra, the mighty asura, with sixty thousand chariots,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.41

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अयुध्यतायुतानां च सहस्रेण महाहनुः। पञ्चाशद्भिश्च नियुतैरसिलोमा महासुरः॥
docs.text: fought on, and Mahāhanu with ten million; and the mighty Asiloman with fifty million,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.42

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अयुतानां शतैः षड्भिर्बाष्कलो युयुधे रणे। गजवाजिसहस्रौघैरनेकैः परिवारितः॥
docs.text: Bāṣkala fought in the battle with six million. Parivārita, with many thousands of elephants and horses in their hosts,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.43

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: वृतो रथानां कोट्या च युद्धे तस्मिन्नयुध्यत। बिडालाख्योऽयुतानां च पञ्चाशद्भिरथायुतैः॥
docs.text: and a crore of chariots about him, fought in that battle. Biḍāla, with fifty ayutas
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.44

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: युयुधे संयुगे तत्र रथानां परिवारितः। अन्ये च तत्रायुतशो रथनागहयैर्वृताः॥
docs.text: of chariots around him, fought in that battle. And other great asuras, each with chariots, elephants and horses by the ten thousand,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.45

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: युयुधुः संयुगे देव्या सह तत्र महासुराः। कोटिकोटिसहस्रैस्तु रथानां दन्तिनां तथा॥
docs.text: fought there in battle against the Goddess. And with thousands upon thousands of crores of chariots and elephants
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.46

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: हयानां च वृतो युद्धे तत्राभून्महिषासुरः। तोमरैर्भिन्दिपालैश्च शक्तिभिर्मुसलैस्तथा॥
docs.text: and horses around him, Mahiṣāsura himself stood in the battle. With javelins and throwing-spears, with lances and clubs
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.47

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: युयुधुः संयुगे देव्या खड्गैः परशुपट्टिशैः। केचिच्च चिक्षिपुः शक्तीः केचित्पाशांस्तथापरे॥
docs.text: With lances and javelins, with spears and maces, with swords, axes and halberds, they fought the Goddess in that battle. Some hurled spears, others nooses; and still others —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.48

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: देवीं खड्गप्रहारैस्तु ते तां हन्तुं प्रचक्रमुः। सापि देवी ततस्तानि शस्त्राण्यस्त्राणि चण्डिका॥
docs.text: set out to cut the Goddess down with blows of the sword. Then the Goddess Caṇḍikā, in her turn, took those weapons and missiles —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.49

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: लीलयैव प्रचिच्छेद निजशस्त्रास्त्रवर्षिणी। अनायस्तानना देवी स्तूयमाना सुरर्षिभिः॥
docs.text: and, raining down her own weapons and missiles, cut them to pieces as if in play. Unwearied of face, praised by gods and seers, the Goddess —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.50

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: मुमोचासुरदेहेषु शस्त्राण्यस्त्राणि चेश्वरी। सोऽपि क्रुद्धो धुतसटो देव्या वाहनकेसरी॥
docs.text: loosed her weapons and missiles upon the asuras’ bodies, sovereign that she is. And her lion too, the Goddess’s own mount, raging and tossing his mane —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.51

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: चचारासुरसैन्येषु वनेष्विव हुताशनः। निःश्वासान् मुमुचे यांश्च युध्यमाना रणेऽम्बिका॥
docs.text: raged through the asura ranks like a fire through the forests. And every breath that Ambikā breathed out as she fought —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.52

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: त एव सद्यः सम्भूता गणाः शतसहस्रशः। युयुधुस्ते परशुभिर्भिन्दिपालासिपट्टिशैः॥
docs.text: became at once her hosts, hundreds of thousands strong. They fought with axes, javelins, swords and halberds,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.53

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: नाशयन्तोऽसुरगणान् देवीशक्त्युपबृंहिताः। अवादयन्त पटहान् गणाः शङ्खांस्तथापरे॥
docs.text: destroying the asura hosts, made mighty by the Goddess’s power. Some of the hosts beat the war-drums, others blew the conches,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.54

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: मृदङ्गांश्च तथैवान्ये तस्मिन् युद्धमहोत्सवे। ततो देवी त्रिशूलेन गदया शक्तिवृष्टिभिः॥
docs.text: and others the mṛdaṅga drums, in that great festival of war. Then the Goddess, with trident and mace and showers of spears,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.55

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: खड्गादिभिश्च शतशो निजघान महासुरान्। पातयामास चैवान्यान् घण्टास्वनविमोहितान्॥
docs.text: with sword and every other weapon, struck down the great asuras by the hundred; and others, dazed by the ringing of her bell, she brought to the ground.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.56

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: असुरान् भुवि पाशेन बद्ध्वा चान्यानकर्षयत्। केचिद् द्विधा कृतास्तीक्ष्णैः खड्गपातैस्तथापरे॥
docs.text: Others she bound with her noose and dragged along the ground. Some were cut in two by the keen strokes of her sword; and others —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.57

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: विपोथिता निपातेन गदया भुवि शेरते। वेमुश्च केचिद्रुधिरं मुसलेन भृशं हताः॥
docs.text: others lie on the ground, crushed by the blows of her mace; and some, struck hard by her club, spewed blood.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.58

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: केचिन्निपतिता भूमौ भिन्नाः शूलेन वक्षसि। निरन्तराः शरौघेण कृताः केचिद्रणाजिरे॥
docs.text: Some, pierced through the chest by her spear, fell to the ground; some, on the field of battle, were riddled through and through by her storm of arrows.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.59

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: श्येनानुकारिणः प्राणान् मुमुचुस्त्रिदशार्दनाः। केषांचिद् बाहवश्छिन्नाश्छिन्नग्रीवास्तथापरे॥
docs.text: Like hawks dropping from the sky, the tormentors of the gods gave up their lives. Some had their arms hewn off, and others their heads struck from their necks.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.60

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: शिरांसि पेतुरन्येषामन्ये मध्ये विदारिताः। विच्छिन्नजङ्घास्त्वपरे पेतुरुर्व्यां महासुराः॥
docs.text: Others’ heads fell; others were split through the middle; and still other great asuras, their legs hewn away, fell to the earth.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.61

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: एकबाह्वक्षिचरणाः केचिद्देव्या द्विधा कृताः। छिन्नेऽपि चान्ये शिरसि पतिताः पुनरुत्थिताः॥
docs.text: Some the Goddess cleft in two, leaving each half one arm, one eye, one foot. And others, though their heads were struck off, fell and rose again —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.62

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: कबन्धा युयुधुर्देव्या गृहीतपरमायुधाः। ननृतुश्चापरे तत्र युद्धे तूर्यलयाश्रिताः॥
docs.text: and fought the Goddess as headless trunks, still gripping their finest weapons; and others danced there on the battlefield to the beat of the war-music.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.63

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: कबन्धाश्छिन्नशिरसः खड्गशक्त्यृष्टिपाणयः। तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति भाषन्तो देवीमन्ये महासुराः॥
docs.text: Other great asuras, headless trunks with their heads struck off, swords and spears and lances still in their hands, kept crying to the Goddess, ‘Stand! Stand and fight!’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.64

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: पातितै रथनागाश्वैरसुरैश्च वसुन्धरा। अगम्या साभवत्तत्र यत्राभूत्स महारणः॥
docs.text: Where that great battle was fought, the earth became impassable, strewn with fallen chariots, elephants, horses and asuras.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.65

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: शोणितौघा महानद्यः सद्यस्तत्र प्रसुस्रुवुः। मध्ये चासुरसैन्यस्य वारणासुरवाजिनाम्॥
docs.text: At once torrents of blood flowed there like great rivers, through the midst of the asura host, among its elephants, warriors and horses.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.66

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: क्षणेन तन्महासैन्यमसुराणां तथाम्बिका। निन्ये क्षयं यथा वह्निस्तृणदारुमहाचयम्॥
docs.text: In a moment Ambikā brought that vast army of the asuras to ruin, as fire consumes a great heap of straw and timber.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.67

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: स च सिंहो महानादमुत्सृजन्धुतकेसरः। शरीरेभ्योऽमरारीणामसूनिव विचिन्वति॥
docs.text: And the lion, shaking his mane and roaring mightily, ranged as if he were plucking the very lives out of the bodies of the gods’ enemies.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.68

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: देव्या गणैश्च तैस्तत्र कृतं युद्धं महासुरैः। यथैषां तुतुषुर्देवाः पुष्पवृष्टिमुचो दिवि॥
docs.text: So the Goddess and her hosts fought the great asuras there, and fought so well that the gods in heaven rejoiced in them and rained down flowers.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 2.69

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: निहन्यमानं तत्सैन्यमवलोक्य महासुरः। सेनानीश्चिक्षुरः कोपाद्ययौ योद्धुमथाम्बिकाम्॥
docs.text: Seeing his army cut down, the mighty asura Cikṣura, Mahiṣa’s general, went in fury to fight Ambikā.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.2

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: स देवीं शरवर्षेण ववर्ष समरेऽसुरः। यथा मेरुगिरेः शृङ्गं तोयवर्षेण तोयदः॥
docs.text: In the battle the asura poured a storm of arrows on the Goddess, as a cloud pours its rain on the summit of Meru.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.3

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तस्यच्छित्त्वा ततो देवी लीलयैव शरोत्करान्। जघान तुरगान् बाणैर्यन्तारं चैव वाजिनाम्॥
docs.text: The Goddess cut his arrows to pieces as if at play, and with her own arrows she killed his horses and their charioteer.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.4

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: चिच्छेद च धनुः सद्यो ध्वजं चातिसमुच्छ्रितम्। विव्याध चैव गात्रेषु छिन्नधन्वानमाशुगैः॥
docs.text: At once she cut through his bow and his towering standard, and with swift arrows she pierced the disarmed asura all over his body.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.5

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सच्छिन्नधन्वा विरथो हताश्वो हतसारथिः। अभ्यधावत तां देवीं खड्गचर्मधरोऽसुरः॥
docs.text: Bow broken, chariot gone, horses and charioteer slain, the asura took up sword and shield and charged at the Goddess.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.6

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सिंहमाहत्य खड्गेन तीक्ष्णधारेण मूर्धनि। आजघान भुजे सव्ये देवीमप्यतिवेगवान्॥
docs.text: Moving with great speed, he struck the lion on the head with his keen-edged sword, and then struck the Goddess herself on her left arm.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.7

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तस्याः खड्गो भुजं प्राप्य पफाल नृपनन्दन। ततो जग्राह शूलं स कोपादरुणलोचनः॥
docs.text: The sword shattered as it met her arm, O prince. Then, his eyes red with rage, he seized a spear.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.8

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: चिक्षेप च ततस्तत्तु भद्रकाल्यां महासुरः। जाज्वल्यमानं तेजोभी रविबिम्बमिवाम्बरात्॥
docs.text: Then the great asura hurled the spear at Bhadrakālī, flaming with light like the sun’s disc falling from the sky.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.9

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: दृष्ट्वा तदापतच्छूलं देवी शूलममुञ्चत। तच्छूलं शतधा तेन नीतं स च महासुरः॥
docs.text: Seeing the spear flying at her, the Goddess hurled her own. It shattered his spear into a hundred pieces — and the great asura with it.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.10

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: हते तस्मिन्महावीर्ये महिषस्य चमूपतौ। आजगाम गजारूढश्चामरस्त्रिदशार्दनः॥
docs.text: When Mahiṣa’s mighty general had fallen, Cāmara, the scourge of the gods, came forward on an elephant.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.11

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सोऽपि शक्तिं मुमोचाथ देव्यास्तामम्बिका द्रुतम्। हुंकाराभिहतां भूमौ पातयामास निष्प्रभाम्॥
docs.text: He in turn hurled a lance at the Goddess; but Ambikā, with a single cry of ‘hum’, struck it down at once, and it fell to the ground, its fire gone out.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.12

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: भग्नां शक्तिं निपतितां दृष्ट्वा क्रोधसमन्वितः। चिक्षेप चामरः शूलं बाणैस्तदपि साच्छिनत्॥
docs.text: Seeing his lance broken on the ground, Cāmara, beside himself with rage, flung a spear; and that too she cut down with her arrows.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.13

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ततः सिंहः समुत्पत्य गजकुम्भान्तरे स्थितः। बाहुयुद्धेन युयुधे तेनोच्चैस्त्रिदशारिणा॥
docs.text: Then the lion sprang up onto the elephant’s brow and, planted there, grappled fiercely with that enemy of the gods.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.14

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: युद्ध्यमानौ ततस्तौ तु तस्मान्नागान्महीं गतौ। युयुधातेऽतिसंरब्धौ प्रहारैरतिदारुणैः॥
docs.text: Locked in combat, the two crashed from the elephant to the ground, and there, in towering rage, fought on with savage blows.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.15

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ततो वेगात् खमुत्पत्य निपत्य च मृगारिणा। करप्रहारेण शिरश्चामरस्य पृथक्कृतम्॥
docs.text: Then the lion sprang swiftly into the air and, coming down, struck off Cāmara’s head with a blow of its paw.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.16

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: उदग्रश्च रणे देव्या शिलावृक्षादिभिर्हतः। दन्तमुष्टितलैश्चैव करालश्च निपातितः॥
docs.text: Udagra was slain in battle by the Goddess with boulders, trees and the like; and Karāla was felled with teeth, fists and blows of the open hand.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.17

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: देवी क्रुद्धा गदापातैश्चूर्णयामास चोद्धतम्। वाष्कलं भिन्दिपालेन बाणैस्ताम्रं तथान्धकम्॥
docs.text: In her fury the Goddess crushed Uddhata with her mace; Bāṣkala she struck down with a javelin, and Tāmra and Andhaka with her arrows.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.18

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: उग्रास्यमुग्रवीर्यं च तथैव च महाहनुम्। त्रिनेत्रा च त्रिशूलेन जघान परमेश्वरी॥
docs.text: And with her trident the three-eyed Supreme Goddess slew Ugrāsya, Ugravīrya and Mahāhanu.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.19

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: बिडालस्यासिना कायात्पातयामास वै शिरः। दुर्धरं दुर्मुखं चोभौ शरैर्निन्ये यमक्षयम्॥
docs.text: With her sword she struck Biḍāla’s head from his body, and with her arrows she sent both Durdhara and Durmukha to the house of Death.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.20

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: एवं संक्षीयमाणे तु स्वसैन्ये महिषासुरः। माहिषेण स्वरूपेण त्रासयामास तान् गणान्॥
docs.text: As his army wasted away, Mahiṣāsura himself, in his own buffalo shape, fell upon the Goddess’s hosts and struck terror into them.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.21

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: कांश्चित्तुण्डप्रहारेण खुरक्षेपैस्तथापरान्। लाङ्गूलताडितांश्चान्याञ्छृङ्गाभ्यां च विदारितान्॥
docs.text: Some he struck down with blows of his muzzle, others with his hooves; others he lashed with his tail, and others he ripped open with his horns —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.22

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: वेगेन कांश्चिदपरान्नादेन भ्रमणेन च। निःश्वासपवनेनान्यान् पातयामास भूतले॥
docs.text: Some he threw to the ground by the force of his charge, others with his bellowing and his wheeling about, and others again with the blast of his breath.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.23

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: निपात्य प्रमथानीकमभ्यधावत सोऽसुरः। सिंहं हन्तुं महादेव्याः कोपं चक्रे ततोऽम्बिका॥
docs.text: Having cut down the Goddess’s host, the demon charged to kill the great Goddess’s lion. At that, Ambikā grew angry.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.24

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सोऽपि कोपान्महावीर्यः खुरक्षुण्णमहीतलः। शृङ्गाभ्यां पर्वतानुच्चांश्चिक्षेप च ननाद च॥
docs.text: He too, in his fury, mighty, churning the earth with his hooves, tossed high mountains with his horns and bellowed.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.25

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: वेगभ्रमणविक्षुण्णा मही तस्य व्यशीर्यत। लाङ्गूलेनाहतश्चाब्धिः प्लावयामास सर्वतः॥
docs.text: Pounded by his charging and wheeling, the earth broke apart; and the ocean, lashed by his tail, overflowed on every side.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.26

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: धुतशृङ्गविभिन्नाश्च खण्डं खण्डं ययुर्घनाः। श्वासानिलास्ताः शतशो निपेतुर्नभसोऽचलाः॥
docs.text: The clouds, torn by his tossing horns, were shredded to pieces, and mountains flung up by the blast of his breath came crashing down from the sky by the hundred.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.27

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: इति क्रोधसमाध्मातमापतन्तं महासुरम्। दृष्ट्वा सा चण्डिका कोपं तद्वधाय तदाकरोत्॥
docs.text: Seeing the great demon bearing down on her, bursting with rage, Caṇḍikā then turned her wrath to his destruction.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.28

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सा क्षिप्त्वा तस्य वै पाशं तं बबन्ध महासुरम्। तत्याज माहिषं रूपं सोऽपि बद्धो महामृधे॥
docs.text: She cast her noose over him and bound the great demon. Caught fast in the great battle, he shed his buffalo form.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.29

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ततः सिंहोऽभवत्सद्यो यावत्तस्याम्बिका शिरः। छिनत्ति तावत्पुरुषः खड्गपाणिरदृश्यत॥
docs.text: At once he became a lion. But just as Ambikā was about to cut off its head, a man appeared, sword in hand.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.30

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तत एवाशु पुरुषं देवी चिच्छेद सायकैः। तं खड्गचर्मणा सार्धं ततः सोऽभून्महागजः॥
docs.text: At that very moment the Goddess cut the man down with her arrows, sword, shield and all. Then he turned into a huge elephant.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.31

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: करेण च महासिंहं तं चकर्ष जगर्ज च। कर्षतस्तु करं देवी खड्गेन निरकृन्तत॥
docs.text: With his trunk he dragged at the great lion, trumpeting; but as he dragged, the Goddess cut off his trunk with her sword.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.32

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ततो महासुरो भूयो माहिषं वपुरास्थितः। तथैव क्षोभयामास त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्॥
docs.text: Then the great demon took on his buffalo body once more and, as before, threw the three worlds into turmoil, all that moves and all that stands still.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.33

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ततः क्रुद्धा जगन्माता चण्डिका पानमुत्तमम्। पपौ पुनः पुनश्चैव जहासारुणलोचना॥
docs.text: Then Caṇḍikā, the Mother of the world, in her fury drank the supreme drink again and again, and laughed, her eyes red.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.34

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ननर्द चासुरः सोऽपि बलवीर्यमदोद्धतः। विषाणाभ्यां च चिक्षेप चण्डिकां प्रति भूधरान्॥
docs.text: The demon, drunk with pride in his strength and valour, roared back and with his horns flung mountains at Caṇḍikā.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.35

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सा च तान् प्रहितांस्तेन चूर्णयन्ती शरोत्करैः। उवाच तं मदोद्धूतमुखरागाकुलाक्षरम्॥
docs.text: Grinding to dust with volleys of arrows the mountains he hurled, she spoke to him, her face flushed with the drink and her words slurred:
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.36

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: गर्ज गर्ज क्षणं मूढ मधु यावत्पिबाम्यहम्। मया त्वयि हतेऽत्रैव गर्जिष्यन्त्याशु देवताः॥
docs.text: Roar, fool, roar on for a moment, while I drink this wine. When I have slain you, it is the gods who will be roaring here — and soon.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.38

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: एवमुक्त्वा समुत्पत्य साऽऽरूढा तं महासुरम्। पादेनाक्रम्य कण्ठे च शूलेनैनमताडयत्॥
docs.text: With these words she leapt up and mounted the great demon; pressing her foot on his neck, she struck him with her spear.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.40

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ततः सोऽपि पदाऽऽक्रान्तस्तया निजमुखात्ततः। अर्धनिष्क्रान्त एवासीद् देव्या वीर्येण संवृतः॥
docs.text: Pinned beneath her foot, the asura began to come forth from the buffalo’s mouth in his own form, but got only halfway, held fast by the Goddess’s power.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.41

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अर्धनिष्क्रान्त एवासौ युध्यमानो महासुरः। तया महासिना देव्या शिरश्छित्त्वा निपातितः॥
docs.text: Still only half emerged, still fighting, the great demon was struck down by the Goddess, who cut off his head with her great sword.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.42

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ततो हाहाकृतं सर्वं दैत्यसैन्यं ननाश तत्। प्रहर्षं च परं जग्मुः सकला देवतागणाः॥
docs.text: Then the whole demon army, wailing, was destroyed, and all the hosts of the gods were filled with the greatest joy.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.43

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तुष्टुवुस्तां सुरा देवीं सह दिव्यैर्महर्षिभिः। जगुर्गन्धर्वपतयो ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः॥
docs.text: The gods, with the heavenly great sages, sang the Goddess’s praise; the Gandharva lords sang and the Apsarases danced.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 3.44

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: शक्रादयः सुरगणा निहतेऽतिवीर्ये तस्मिन्दुरात्मनि सुरारिबले च देव्या। तां तुष्टुवुः प्रणतिनम्रशिरोधरांसा वाग्भिः प्रहर्षपुलकोद्गमचारुदेहाः॥
docs.text: When the Devī had slain that mighty, evil-hearted one and the army of the gods’ enemies, Indra and the hosts of the gods, necks and shoulders bowed in reverence, their bodies thrilling with joy, praised her in words.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.2

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: देव्या यया ततमिदं जगदात्मशक्त्या निश्शेषदेवगणशक्तिसमूहमूर्त्या। तामम्बिकामखिलदेवमहर्षिपूज्यां भक्त्या नताः स्म विदधातु शुभानि सा नः॥
docs.text: To Ambikā, worshipped by all the gods and great sages — the Devī who by her own power pervades this world, her form the gathered powers of all the hosts of gods — we bow in devotion. May she grant us what is good.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.3

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: यस्याः प्रभावमतुलं भगवाननन्तो ब्रह्मा हरश्च न हि वक्तुमलं बलं च। सा चण्डिकाखिलजगत्परिपालनाय नाशाय चाशुभभयस्य मतिं करोतु॥
docs.text: Her incomparable majesty and strength not even blessed Viṣṇu, Brahmā or Śiva can describe. May that Caṇḍikā turn her mind to protecting the whole world and to ending evil and fear.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.4

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: या श्रीः स्वयं सुकृतिनां भवनेष्वलक्ष्मीः पापात्मनां कृतधियां हृदयेषु बुद्धिः। श्रद्धा सतां कुलजनप्रभवस्य लज्जा तां त्वां नताः स्म परिपालय देवि विश्वम्॥
docs.text: You are Fortune herself in the homes of the virtuous and Misfortune in the homes of the wicked; understanding in the hearts of the wise, faith in the good, modesty in the well-born. To you we bow: O Devī, protect the world.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.5

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: किं वर्णयाम तव रूपमचिन्त्यमेतत् किं चातिवीर्यमसुरक्षयकारि भूरि। किं चाहवेषु चरितानि तवाद्भुतानि सर्वेषु देव्यसुरदेवगणादिकेषु॥
docs.text: How can we describe this form of yours, beyond all thought? Or your boundless valour that destroys the asuras? Or the wonders you have done in battle, O Devī, among all the hosts of gods, asuras and others?
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.6

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: हेतुः समस्तजगतां त्रिगुणापि दोषै- र्न ज्ञायसे हरिहरादिभिरप्यपारा। सर्वाश्रयाखिलमिदं जगदंशभूत- मव्याकृता हि परमा प्रकृतिस्त्वमाद्या॥
docs.text: You are the cause of all the worlds. Though you bear the three guṇas, no fault of theirs is found in you; even Viṣṇu, Śiva and the other gods cannot reach your farther shore. You are the support of all, and this whole world is but a portion of you, for you are the primal Prakṛti, supreme and unmanifest.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.7

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: यस्याः समस्तसुरता समुदीरणेन तृप्तिं प्रयाति सकलेषु मखेषु देवि। स्वाहासि वै पितृगणस्य च तृप्तिहेतु- रुच्चार्यसे त्वमत एव जनैः स्वधा च॥
docs.text: O Devī, at every sacrifice it is by the uttering of you that all the gods together are satisfied: you are Svāhā. And because you satisfy the host of the ancestors, people utter you as Svadhā.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.8

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: या मुक्तिहेतुरविचिन्त्यमहाव्रता त्व- मभ्यस्यसे सुनियतेन्द्रियतत्त्वसारैः। मोक्षार्थिभिर्मुनिभिरस्तसमस्तदोषै- र्विद्यासि सा भगवती परमा हि देवि॥
docs.text: You are the cause of liberation, your great discipline beyond thought. Sages who seek release — senses held in check, intent on the truth, every fault cast off — make you their practice. You, O Devī, are that blessed and supreme Knowledge.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.9

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: शब्दात्मिका सुविमलर्ग्यजुषां निधान- मुद्गीथरम्यपदपाठवतां च साम्नाम्। देवी त्रयी भगवती भवभावनाय वार्ता च सर्वजगतां परमार्तिहन्त्री॥
docs.text: Your very self is sound: you are the treasure-house of the spotless Ṛk and Yajus and of the Sāman chants, lovely in their words with the udgītha. Blessed Devī, you are the Triple Veda, for the sustaining of the world, and you are Vārttā, the livelihood that ends the deepest distress of all the worlds.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.10

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: मेधासि देवि विदिताखिलशास्त्रसारा दुर्गासि दुर्गभवसागरनौरसङ्गा। श्रीः कैटभारिहृदयैककृताधिवासा गौरी त्वमेव शशिमौलिकृतप्रतिष्ठा॥
docs.text: O Devī, you are Medhā, who knows the essence of every scripture; you are Durgā, the boat across the perilous ocean of worldly life, yourself untouched by attachment. You are Śrī, whose one dwelling is the heart of Viṣṇu, Kaiṭabha’s foe; and you alone are Gaurī, established with the moon-crowned Śiva.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.11

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ईषत्सहासममलं परिपूर्णचन्द्र- बिम्बानुकारि कनकोत्तमकान्तिकान्तम्। अत्यद्भुतं प्रहृतमात्तरुषा तथापि वक्त्रं विलोक्य सहसा महिषासुरेण॥
docs.text: Your face was gently smiling and spotless, like the orb of the full moon, lovely with the glow of finest gold; that Mahiṣāsura could look on it and even so, seized by fury, strike out at once — that is a great wonder.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.12

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: दृष्ट्वा तु देवि कुपितं भ्रुकुटीकराल- मुद्यच्छशाङ्कसदृशच्छवि यन्न सद्यः। प्राणान्मुमोच महिषस्तदतीव चित्रं कैर्जीव्यते हि कुपितान्तकदर्शनेन॥
docs.text: But, O Devī, Mahiṣa saw your face in anger — dreadful with its frown, flushed like the rising moon — and did not die on the spot: that is the stranger wonder. For who can live once he has looked on Death enraged?
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.13

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: देवि प्रसीद परमा भवती भवाय सद्यो विनाशयसि कोपवती कुलानि। विज्ञातमेतदधुनैव यदस्तमेत- न्नीतं बलं सुविपुलं महिषासुरस्य॥
docs.text: Be gracious, O Devī! Supreme, you are there for our flourishing; in anger you destroy whole races in a moment. We have seen it just now: the vast army of Mahiṣāsura has been brought to nothing.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.14

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ते सम्मता जनपदेषु धनानि तेषां तेषां यशांसि न च सीदति धर्मवर्गः। धन्यास्त एव निभृतात्मजभृत्यदारा येषां सदाभ्युदयदा भवती प्रसन्ना॥
docs.text: Those to whom you, the giver of prosperity, are always gracious are honoured in every land. Wealth is theirs, and fame, and their righteousness never fails. Blessed are they, and loyal their sons, their servants and their wives.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.15

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: धर्म्याणि देवि सकलानि सदैव कर्मा- ण्यत्यादृतः प्रतिदिनं सुकृती करोति। स्वर्गं प्रयाति च ततो भवतीप्रसादा- ल्लोकत्रयेऽपि फलदा ननु देवि तेन॥
docs.text: O Devī, the virtuous man performs every righteous deed, day after day, with devoted care, and then by your grace he goes to heaven. So is it not you, O Devī, who give the fruit of action in all three worlds?
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.16

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: दुर्गे स्मृता हरसि भीतिमशेषजन्तोः स्वस्थैः स्मृता मतिमतीव शुभां ददासि। दारिद्र्यदुःखभयहारिणि का त्वदन्या सर्वोपकारकरणाय सदाऽऽर्द्रचित्ता॥
docs.text: O Durgā, when you are remembered you take away the fear of every creature; remembered by those at ease, you give a mind turned wholly to the good. Remover of poverty, sorrow and fear — who but you has a heart ever tender, ready to help all?
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.17

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: एभिर्हतैर्जगदुपैति सुखं तथैते कुर्वन्तु नाम नरकाय चिराय पापम्। संग्राममृत्युमधिगम्य दिवं प्रयान्तु मत्वेति नूनमहितान् विनिहंसि देवि॥
docs.text: ‘With these slain, the world will find happiness; and though they have earned a long hell by their sins, let them meet death in battle and go to heaven’ — surely it is with this thought, O Devī, that you strike your enemies down.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.18

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: दृष्ट्वैव किं न भवती प्रकरोति भस्म सर्वासुरानरिषु यत्प्रहिणोषि शस्त्रम्। लोकान् प्रयान्तु रिपवोऽपि हि शस्त्रपूता इत्थं मतिर्भवति तेष्वपि तेऽतिसाध्वी॥
docs.text: Why do you not burn all the asuras to ash with a single glance, but hurl your weapons at them instead? Because you would have even your enemies, made pure by your weapons, reach the higher worlds. So kind is your intent, even towards them.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.19

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: खड्गप्रभानिकरविस्फुरणैस्तथोग्रैः शूलाग्रकान्तिनिवहेन दृशोऽसुराणाम्। यन्नागता विलयमंशुमदिन्दुखण्ड- योग्याननं तव विलोकयतां तदेतत्॥
docs.text: The blazing flashes of your sword and the flood of light from the point of your trident did not destroy the asuras’ eyes — because they were gazing at your face, like the radiant crescent of the moon.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.20

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: दुर्वृत्तवृत्तशमनं तव देवि शीलं रूपं तथैतदविचिन्त्यमतुल्यमन्यैः। वीर्यं च हन्तृ हृतदेवपराक्रमाणां वैरिष्वपि प्रकटितैव दया त्वयेत्थम्॥
docs.text: O Devī, it is your nature to put an end to the ways of the wicked; your form is beyond thought, and none can equal it; your valour destroys those who robbed the gods of their might — and in this way you have shown compassion even to your enemies.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.21

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: केनोपमा भवतु तेऽस्य पराक्रमस्य रूपं च शत्रुभयकार्यतिहारि कुत्र। चित्ते कृपा समरनिष्ठुरता च दृष्टा त्वय्येव देवि वरदे भुवनत्रयेऽपि॥
docs.text: To what could this valour of yours be compared? Where else is a form that strikes terror into enemies and yet captivates the heart? Compassion within and relentlessness in battle — in all three worlds, O Devī, giver of boons, these are seen together in you alone.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.22

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: त्रैलोक्यमेतदखिलं रिपुनाशनेन त्रातं त्वया समरमूर्धनि तेऽपि हत्वा। नीता दिवं रिपुगणा भयमप्यपास्त- मस्माकमुन्मदसुरारिभवं नमस्ते॥
docs.text: By destroying the enemies you have saved these three worlds entire. Slaying them at the forefront of battle, you have led even those enemy hosts to heaven; and you have driven away our fear of the frenzied foes of the gods. Salutation to you!
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.23

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: शूलेन पाहि नो देवि पाहि खड्गेन चाम्बिके। घण्टास्वनेन नः पाहि चापज्यानिःस्वनेन च॥
docs.text: Protect us with your trident, O Devī; protect us with your sword, O Mother; protect us with the ringing of your bell and the twang of your bowstring.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.24

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: प्राच्यां रक्ष प्रतीच्यां च चण्डिके रक्ष दक्षिणे। भ्रामणेनात्मशूलस्य उत्तरस्यां तथेश्वरि॥
docs.text: Protect us in the east and in the west, O Caṇḍikā; protect us in the south; and in the north as well, O Sovereign Lady, by the whirling of your trident.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.25

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सौम्यानि यानि रूपाणि त्रैलोक्ये विचरन्ति ते। यानि चात्यर्थघोराणि तै रक्षास्मांस्तथा भुवम्॥
docs.text: With all your forms that roam the three worlds, the gentle ones and those terrible beyond measure, protect us, and the earth as well.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.26

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: खड्गशूलगदादीनि यानि चास्त्राणि तेऽम्बिके। करपल्लवसङ्गीनि तैरस्मान् रक्ष सर्वतः॥
docs.text: And with all your weapons, O Mother — sword, trident, mace and the rest — that rest in your tender hands, protect us on every side.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.27

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: एवं स्तुता सुरैर्दिव्यैः कुसुमैर्नन्दनोद्भवैः। अर्चिता जगतां धात्री तथा गन्धानुलेपनैः॥
docs.text: Praised in this way by the gods, and honoured with heavenly flowers from the garden of Nandana, with perfumes and with fragrant pastes, the Mother of the worlds —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.29

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: भक्त्या समस्तैस्त्रिदशैर्दिव्यैर्धूपैस्तु धूपिता। प्राह प्रसादसुमुखी समस्तान् प्रणतान् सुरान्॥
docs.text: and when all the gods had devoutly offered her heavenly incense, she, her face bright with grace, spoke to the whole company of gods as they bowed before her.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.30

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: व्रियतां त्रिदशाः सर्वे यदस्मत्तोऽभिवाञ्छितम्॥
docs.text: All you gods, choose whatever you desire of me.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.32

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: भगवत्या कृतं सर्वं न किंचिदवशिष्यते॥
docs.text: You, Blessed One, have done everything; nothing is left to be done.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.34

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: यदयं निहतः शत्रुरस्माकं महिषासुरः। यदि चापि वरो देयस्त्वयास्माकं महेश्वरि॥
docs.text: for Mahiṣāsura, our enemy, lies slain. Yet if you would still grant us a boon, O Supreme Sovereign, —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.35

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: संस्मृता संस्मृता त्वं नो हिंसेथाः परमापदः। यश्च मर्त्यः स्तवैरेभिस्त्वां स्तोष्यत्यमलानने॥
docs.text: whenever we call you to mind, destroy our worst calamities. And whoever among mortals praises you with these hymns, O Goddess of the stainless face, —
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.36

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तस्य वित्तर्द्धिविभवैर्धनदारादिसम्पदाम्। वृद्धयेऽस्मत्प्रसन्ना त्वं भवेथाः सर्वदाम्बिके॥
docs.text: may you, O Mother, ever gracious to us, be with that person always, to increase his wealth, prosperity and fortune, his riches, his wife and family, and all he has.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.37

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: इति प्रसादिता देवैर्जगतोऽर्थे तथाऽऽत्मनः। तथेत्युक्त्वा भद्रकाली बभूवान्तर्हिता नृप॥
docs.text: So the gods entreated her, for the world’s sake and for their own; and Bhadrakālī said, ‘So be it,’ and vanished from their sight, O king.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.39

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: इत्येतत्कथितं भूप सम्भूता सा यथा पुरा। देवीदेवशरीरेभ्यो जगत्त्रयहितैषिणी॥
docs.text: So, O king, I have told you how long ago the Goddess, who seeks the good of the three worlds, came forth from the bodies of the gods.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.40

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: पुनश्च गौरीदेहात्सा समुद्भूता यथाभवत्। वधाय दुष्टदैत्यानां तथा शुम्भनिशुम्भयोः॥
docs.text: and how once more she arose, this time from the body of Gaurī, to slay the wicked Daityas, and Śumbha and Niśumbha with them,
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.41

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: रक्षणाय च लोकानां देवानामुपकारिणी। तच्छृणुष्व मयाऽऽख्यातं यथावत्कथयामि ते॥
docs.text: and to protect the worlds, ever the helper of the gods. Listen as I tell it; I shall tell it to you just as it happened.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 4.42

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: पुरा शुम्भनिशुम्भाभ्यामसुराभ्यां शचीपतेः। त्रैलोक्यं यज्ञभागाश्च हृता मदबलाश्रयात्॥
docs.text: Long ago the asuras Śumbha and Niśumbha, trusting in their pride and their strength, seized from Indra, Śacī’s lord, the three worlds and his share of the sacrifices.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.2

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तावेव सूर्यतां तद्वदधिकारं तथैन्दवम्। कौबेरमथ याम्यं च चक्राते वरुणस्य च॥
docs.text: They seized for themselves the Sun’s place, and in the same way the offices of the Moon, of Kubera, of Yama and of Varuṇa.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.3

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तावेव पवनर्द्धिं च चक्रतुर्वह्निकर्म च। ततो देवा विनिर्धूता भ्रष्टराज्याः पराजिताः॥
docs.text: They took the Wind’s power too, and the office of Fire. So the gods, defeated and stripped of their kingdom, were cast out.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.4

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: हृताधिकारास्त्रिदशास्ताभ्यां सर्वे निराकृताः। महासुराभ्यां तां देवीं संस्मरन्त्यपराजिताम्॥
docs.text: Robbed of their offices and driven out by the two great asuras, all the gods turned their minds to that Goddess, the Unconquered One.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.5

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तयास्माकं वरो दत्तो यथाऽऽपत्सु स्मृताखिलाः। भवतां नाशयिष्यामि तत्क्षणात्परमापदः॥
docs.text: She gave us a boon: ‘When I am remembered in your misfortunes, I will that very instant destroy all your direst calamities.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.6

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: इति कृत्वा मतिं देवा हिमवन्तं नगेश्वरम्। जग्मुस्तत्र ततो देवीं विष्णुमायां प्रतुष्टुवुः॥
docs.text: Resolved on this, the gods went to the Himālaya, king of mountains, and there they sang the praises of the Goddess, Viṣṇumāyā.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.7

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: नमो देव्यै महादेव्यै शिवायै सततं नमः। नमः प्रकृत्यै भद्रायै नियताः प्रणताः स्म ताम्॥
docs.text: Homage to the Goddess, to the Great Goddess; to the Auspicious One, homage for ever. Homage to Nature, the Primal One, to the Gracious One. With minds held still we bow before her.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.9

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: रौद्रायै नमो नित्यायै गौर्यै धात्र्यै नमो नमः। ज्योत्स्नायै चेन्दुरूपिण्यै सुखायै सततं नमः॥
docs.text: Homage to the Fierce One; homage and homage to the Eternal, to Gaurī, to her who upholds all. To the Moonlight, to her whose form is the Moon, to Joy itself, homage for ever.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.10

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: कल्याण्यै प्रणतां वृद्ध्यै सिद्ध्यै कुर्मो नमो नमः। नैर्ऋत्यै भूभृतां लक्ष्म्यै शर्वाण्यै ते नमो नमः॥
docs.text: To the Auspicious One, who is the increase and the fulfilment of all who bow to her, we offer homage and homage. To Nairṛtī, to the royal fortune of kings, to Śarvāṇī — to you, homage and homage.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.11

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: दुर्गायै दुर्गपारायै सारायै सर्वकारिण्यै। ख्यात्यै तथैव कृष्णायै धूम्रायै सततं नमः॥
docs.text: To Durgā, who brings us across every hardship; to the Essence, the Maker of all; to Renown, to the Dark One, to the Smoke-hued: homage for ever.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.12

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अतिसौम्यातिरौद्रायै नतास्तस्यै नमो नमः। नमो जगत्प्रतिष्ठायै देव्यै कृत्यै नमो नमः॥
docs.text: Bowing, we offer homage and homage to her who is at once most gentle and most terrible. Homage to the ground on which the world stands, to the Goddess, to Action itself: homage, homage.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.13

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु विष्णुमायेति शब्दिता। नमस्तस्यै। १४। नमस्तस्यै। १५। नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः॥
docs.text: To the Goddess who in all beings is named Viṣṇu’s Māyā: homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.14–16

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु चेतनेत्यभिधीयते। नमस्तस्यै। १७। नमस्तस्यै। १८। नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः॥
docs.text: To the Goddess who in all beings is called Consciousness: homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.17–19

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु बुद्धिरूपेण संस्थिता। नमस्तस्यै। २०। नमस्तस्यै। २१। नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः॥
docs.text: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as Intelligence: homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.20–22

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु निद्रारूपेण संस्थिता। नमस्तस्यै। २३। नमस्तस्यै। २४। नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः॥
docs.text: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as Sleep: homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.23–25

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु क्षुधारूपेण संस्थिता। नमस्तस्यै। २६। नमस्तस्यै। २७। नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः॥
docs.text: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as Hunger: homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.26–28

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: या देवी सर्वभूतेषुच्छायारूपेण संस्थिता। नमस्तस्यै। २९। नमस्तस्यै। ३०। नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः॥
docs.text: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as Shadow: homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.29–31

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam

docs.text: To the Goddess who rules the senses and the elements, and who ever pervades all beings — to her, the all-pervading Goddess, salutation again and again.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.77

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam

docs.text: To her who, as consciousness, pervades this whole world and abides in it: salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her — salutation again and again.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.78–80

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: स्तुता सुरैः पूर्वमभीष्टसंश्रया- त्तथा सुरेन्द्रेण दिनेषु सेविता। करोतु सा नः शुभहेतुरीश्वरी शुभानि भद्राण्यभिहन्तु चापदः॥
docs.text: She whom the gods once praised when their desire was granted, and whom Indra, lord of the gods, worshipped day after day — may that Sovereign, the source of all good, bring us what is auspicious and blessed, and strike down our calamities.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.81

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: या साम्प्रतं चोद्धतदैत्यतापितै- रस्माभिरीशा च सुरैर्नमस्यते। या च स्मृता तत्क्षणमेव हन्ति नः सर्वापदो भक्तिविनम्रमूर्तिभिः॥
docs.text: She to whom we gods, harried by the arrogant daityas, now bow as Sovereign, and who, the moment she is remembered by those bowed down in devotion, destroys all our calamities — (may she bring us good).
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.82

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: एवं स्तवादियुक्तानां देवानां तत्र पार्वती। स्नातुमभ्याययौ तोये जाह्नव्या नृपनन्दन॥
docs.text: While the gods were thus praising, O prince, Pārvatī came there to bathe in the waters of the Gaṅgā.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.84

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: साब्रवीत्तान् सुरान् सुभ्रूर्भवद्भिः स्तूयतेऽत्र का। शरीरकोशतश्चास्याः समुद्भूताब्रवीच्छिवा॥
docs.text: The lovely-browed Goddess asked the gods, ‘Whom are you praising here?’ And from the sheath of her own body Śivā came forth and answered:
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.85

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: स्तोत्रं ममैतत् क्रियते शुम्भदैत्यनिराकृतैः। देवैः समेतैः समरे निशुम्भेन पराजितैः॥
docs.text: ‘This hymn is offered to me by the gods, who have gathered here after the demon Śumbha drove them out and Niśumbha defeated them in battle.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.86

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: शरीरकोशाद्यत्तस्याः पार्वत्या निःसृताम्बिका। कौशिकीति समस्तेषु ततो लोकेषु गीयते॥
docs.text: Because Ambikā emerged from the sheath of Pārvatī’s body, she is celebrated in all the worlds as Kauśikī.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.87

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तस्यां विनिर्गतायां तु कृष्णाभूत्सापि पार्वती। कालिकेति समाख्याता हिमाचलकृताश्रया॥
docs.text: When Ambikā had come forth, Pārvatī herself turned dark. Known as Kālikā, she took up her abode on the Himālaya.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.88

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ततोऽम्बिकां परं रूपं बिभ्राणां सुमनोहरम्। ददर्श चण्डो मुण्डश्च भृत्यौ शुम्भनिशुम्भयोः॥
docs.text: Then Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, servants of Śumbha and Niśumbha, saw Ambikā in her surpassing, enchanting beauty.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.89

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ताभ्यां शुम्भाय चाख्याता अतीव सुमनोहरा। काप्यास्ते स्त्री महाराज भासयन्ती हिमाचलम्॥
docs.text: They told Śumbha of her: ‘Great king, there is a woman of surpassing beauty dwelling on the Himālaya, lighting up the mountain.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.90

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: नैव तादृक् क्वचिद्रूपं दृष्टं केनचिदुत्तमम्। ज्ञायतां काप्यसौ देवी गृह्यतां चासुरेश्वर॥
docs.text: ‘Never has anyone, anywhere, seen beauty so perfect. Find out who this goddess may be, lord of the asuras, and take her.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.91

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: स्त्रीरत्नमतिचार्वङ्गी द्योतयन्ती दिशस्त्विषा। सा तु तिष्ठति दैत्येन्द्र तां भवान् द्रष्टुमर्हति॥
docs.text: ‘A jewel among women, perfect in every limb, she lights the whole horizon with her splendour. There she stays, lord of the demons — you should see her.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.92

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: यानि रत्नानि मणयो गजाश्वादीनि वै प्रभो। त्रैलोक्ये तु समस्तानि साम्प्रतं भान्ति ते गृहे॥
docs.text: ‘Lord, every treasure of the three worlds — jewels, gems, elephants, horses and all the rest — now shines in your palace.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.93

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: ऐरावतः समानीतो गजरत्नं पुरन्दरात्। पारिजाततरुश्चायं तथैवोच्चैःश्रवा हयः॥
docs.text: ‘Airāvata, finest of elephants, has been taken from Indra; so too this Pārijāta tree, and the horse Uccaiḥśravas.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.94

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: विमानं हंससंयुक्तमेतत्तिष्ठति तेऽङ्गणे। रत्नभूतमिहानीतं यदासीद्वेधसोऽद्भुतम्॥
docs.text: ‘In your courtyard stands this swan-drawn chariot of the skies, a true treasure brought here — once the marvel of Brahmā.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.95

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: निधिरेष महापद्मः समानीतो धनेश्वरात्। किञ्जल्किनीं ददौ चाब्धिर्मालामम्लानपङ्कजाम्॥
docs.text: ‘This treasure, the Mahāpadma, was taken from Kubera; and the Ocean gave you a garland of never-fading lotuses, fresh with their filaments.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.96

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: छत्रं ते वारुणं गेहे काञ्चनस्रावि तिष्ठति। तथायं स्यन्दनवरो यः पुराऽऽसीत्प्रजापतेः॥
docs.text: ‘Varuṇa’s parasol, raining gold, stands in your palace, and so does this superb chariot that once belonged to Prajāpati.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.97

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: मृत्योरुत्क्रान्तिदा नाम शक्तिरीश त्वया हृता। पाशः सलिलराजस्य भ्रातुस्तव परिग्रहे॥
docs.text: ‘You have taken, lord, Death’s spear called Utkrāntidā; and the noose of Varuṇa, king of the waters, is held by your brother.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.98

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: निशुम्भस्याब्धिजाताश्च समस्ता रत्नजातयः। वह्निरपि ददौ तुभ्यमग्निशौचे च वाससी॥
docs.text: ‘Every kind of gem the ocean yields belongs to Niśumbha; and even Agni has given you two garments purified by fire.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.99

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: एवं दैत्येन्द्र रत्नानि समस्तान्याहृतानि ते। स्त्रीरत्नमेषा कल्याणी त्वया कस्मान्न गृह्यते॥
docs.text: ‘So, lord of the demons, every treasure has been brought to you. Why then do you not take this lovely one, the jewel among women?’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.100

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: निशम्येति वचः शुम्भः स तदा चण्डमुण्डयोः। प्रेषयामास सुग्रीवं दूतं देव्या महासुरम्॥
docs.text: Hearing what Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa said, Śumbha sent the mighty demon Sugrīva as his envoy to the Goddess.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.102

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: इति चेति च वक्तव्या सा गत्वा वचनान्मम। यथा चाभ्येति सम्प्रीत्या तथा कार्यं त्वया लघु॥
docs.text: ‘Go to her and tell her this and this from me; and act quickly, so that she comes to me willingly.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.103

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: स तत्र गत्वा यत्रास्ते शैलोद्देशेऽतिशोभने। सा देवी तां ततः प्राह श्लक्ष्णं मधुरया गिरा॥
docs.text: Sugrīva went to the lovely mountain slope where the Goddess was staying, and addressed her gently, in honeyed words.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.104

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: देवि दैत्येश्वरः शुम्भस्त्रैलोक्ये परमेश्वरः। दूतोऽहं प्रेषितस्तेन त्वत्सकाशमिहागतः॥
docs.text: ‘Goddess, Śumbha, lord of the demons, is supreme sovereign of the three worlds. I am his envoy, sent by him, and have come here before you.’
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.106

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अव्याहताज्ञः सर्वासु यः सदा देवयोनिषु। निर्जिताखिलदैत्यारिः स यदाह शृणुष्व तत्॥
docs.text: Among all the orders of heavenly beings his command is never resisted, and he has vanquished every foe of the Daityas. Hear what he says.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.107

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: मम त्रैलोक्यमखिलं मम देवा वशानुगाः। यज्ञभागानहं सर्वानुपाश्नामि पृथक् पृथक्॥
docs.text: “The three worlds are mine entire, and the gods obey my will. Every share of the sacrifice, one by one, is mine to enjoy.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.108

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: त्रैलोक्ये वररत्नानि मम वश्यान्यशेषतः। तथैव गजरत्नं च हृत्वा देवेन्द्रवाहनम्॥
docs.text: Every treasure of worth in the three worlds belongs to me, without exception — so too the king of elephants, Indra’s own mount, which I have taken.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.109

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: क्षीरोदमथनोद्भूतमश्वरत्नं ममामरैः। उच्चैःश्रवससंज्ञं तत्प्रणिपत्य समर्पितम्॥
docs.text: Uccaiḥśravas, the finest of horses, born from the churning of the Ocean of Milk, the gods themselves surrendered to me with bowed heads.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.110

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: यानि चान्यानि देवेषु गन्धर्वेषूरगेषु च। रत्नभूतानि भूतानि तानि मय्येव शोभने॥
docs.text: And whatever else ranks as a jewel among gods, Gandharvas and serpents — all of it, lovely one, rests with me alone.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.111

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: स्त्रीरत्नभूतां त्वां देवि लोके मन्यामहे वयम्। सा त्वमस्मानुपागच्छ यतो रत्नभुजो वयम्॥
docs.text: We hold you, O Devī, to be the jewel among the women of the world. Come to us, then, for jewels are ours to enjoy.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.112

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: मां वा ममानुजं वापि निशुम्भमुरुविक्रमम्। भज त्वं चञ्चलापाङ्गि रत्नभूतासि वै यतः॥
docs.text: Take me, or my younger brother Niśumbha of mighty valour, O lady of the darting glance — for a jewel is what you are.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.113

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: परमैश्वर्यमतुलं प्राप्स्यसे मत्परिग्रहात्। एतद् बुद्ध्या समालोच्य मत्परिग्रहतां व्रज॥
docs.text: As my wife you will gain a sovereignty beyond compare. Weigh this well in your mind, and become my consort.”
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.114

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: इत्युक्ता सा तदा देवी गम्भीरान्तःस्मिता जगौ। दुर्गा भगवती भद्रा ययेदं धार्यते जगत्॥
docs.text: So addressed, the Devī — Durgā, the Blessed, the Auspicious, by whom this world is upheld — grave of face yet smiling inwardly, gave her answer.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.116

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: सत्यमुक्तं त्वया नात्र मिथ्या किञ्चित्त्वयोदितम्। त्रैलोक्याधिपतिः शुम्भो निशुम्भश्चापि तादृशः॥
docs.text: What you say is true; you have spoken no falsehood here. Śumbha is lord of the three worlds, and Niśumbha is his equal.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.118

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: किं त्वत्र यत्प्रतिज्ञातं मिथ्या तत्क्रियते कथम्। श्रूयतामल्पबुद्धित्वात्प्रतिज्ञा या कृता पुरा॥
docs.text: But in this matter there is a vow I made, and how could I break it? Hear the promise I once made, foolishly.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.119

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: यो मां जयति संग्रामे यो मे दर्पं व्यपोहति। यो मे प्रतिबलो लोके स मे भर्ता भविष्यति॥
docs.text: “He who conquers me in battle, who humbles my pride, who is my equal in strength in all the world — he shall be my husband.”
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.120

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: तदागच्छतु शुम्भोऽत्र निशुम्भो वा महासुरः। मां जित्वा किं चिरेणात्र पाणिं गृह्णातु मे लघु॥
docs.text: So let Śumbha come here, or Niśumbha, the mighty asura. Let him conquer me and, without delay, take my hand.
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.121

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अवलिप्तासि मैवं त्वं देवि ब्रूहि ममाग्रतः। त्रैलोक्ये कः पुमांस्तिष्ठेदग्रे शुम्भनिशुम्भयोः॥
docs.text: You are proud, O Devī. Do not speak so in my presence. What man in the three worlds could stand before Śumbha and Niśumbha?
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.123

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: अन्येषामपि दैत्यानां सर्वे देवा न वै युधि। तिष्ठन्ति सम्मुखे देवि किं पुनः स्त्री त्वमेकिका॥
docs.text: Not all the gods together can stand in battle even before the lesser Daityas, O Devī — how much less you, a woman, alone!
docs.title: Devī Māhātmyam 5.124

docs.subtitle: Sacred text · Devī Māhātmyam
tags: इन्द्राद्याः सकला देवास्तस्थुर्येषां न संयुगे। शुम्भादीनां कथं तेषां स्त्री प्रयास्यसि सम्मुखम्॥
